serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: Beam is a browser-based SaaS platform for human services agencies. Notes records staff conversations and produces an AI transcript and summary against customer-defined templates; a human reviews, edits, and copies the output into the customer's case management system; Reports, a function within Notes, summarizes uploaded documents, recordings, handwritten notes, video, or existing Notes into a report against a customer template. Talk is a conversational AI voice and chat agent that answers resident calls and chats, with SIP transfer to a human agent on triage need, safeguarding risk, or explicit request. Interpret provides real-time interpretation, combining speech-to-text, LLM interpretation, and text-to-speech, through a browser interface or over a telephone path. The US deployment is standalone: customer data is stored and processed entirely within the continental United States, in US data centers, with backups stored in US data centers.

For the period April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026, CertPro CPA LLC examined
ConnectSecure LLC's ConnectSecure Vulnerability and Compliance
Manager system. In the service auditor's opinion, in all material respects
and based on the applicable Trust Services Criteria for Security, Availability,
and Confidentiality: (1) the description fairly presents the system that was
designed and implemented throughout the period; (2) the controls were
suitably designed to provide reasonable assurance that ConnectSecure's
service commitments and system requirements would be achieved if the
controls operated effectively, and if the subservice organizations and user
entities applied the complementary controls contemplated in the design;
and (3) the controls operated effectively throughout the period. This is an
unqualified opinion with no exceptions noted.

alternativeSecurityFramework.mappingToFedRampRules:
This SOC 2 Type II examination was performed by CertPro CPA LLC under
AICPA attestation standards (AT-C) for the period April 1, 2025 – March 31,
2026, against the 2017 Trust Services Criteria (with 2022 revised points of
focus) for Security, Availability, and Confidentiality. It covered the Common
Criteria (CC1–CC9: control environment, communication and information,
risk assessment, monitoring, control activities, logical and physical access,
system operations, change management, and risk mitigation) plus the
Availability (A1) and Confidentiality (C1) criteria. These map to core
FedRAMP/NIST SP 800-53 control families — Access Control (AC),
Identification & Authentication (IA), Audit & Accountability (AU),
Configuration Management (CM), Contingency Planning (CP), Incident
Response (IR), Risk Assessment (RA), System & Communications
Protection (SC), and System & Information Integrity (SI). The auditor issued
an unqualified opinion: controls were suitably designed and operated
effectively throughout the period with no exceptions noted, and no material
incidents or availability breaches occurred. Independent web-application and
thick-client penetration testing was performed by BDO India LLP
(CREST-accredited) in January 2026, with all findings remediated and
verified closed by February 10, 2026.

It operationalizes documented protocols rather than introducing new treatment methods.

trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions:
**Portal access.** Access is granted through a User Access Request (UAR). Your sponsor or point of contact submits the UAR from the Trust Center portal under Request Services; an approver reviews it and the request is tracked as an auditable ticket. Access is removed the same way. You may also self-register from the portal login page (Create New User Account) — a self-registered account is associated with your organization when your email domain matches — but UAR approval is still required before certification data is released. Accounts are role-based and scoped to this system; sensitive fields are excluded from shared reports.

**Programmatic access.** There is no self-service token flow. Submit a service request under Request Services on the same UAR path. Elvo then issues a Client ID and Client Secret scoped to your organization and system, your base URL and tenant identifier, the report ids your organization may pull, and the document retrieval endpoints. Authentication is OAuth2 client_credentials.

**Full instructions:** https://grcitsm.stratuscyber.com/trust-center-access-guide/

The tenant is configured and operated for Elvo by Stratus Cyber LLC. Elvo uses a FedRAMP Certified platform for certification data sharing rather than building and certifying its own. Halo is FedRAMP Certified under package ID FR2621445678 (Type 20x, Path Program, Class C (Moderate), certified 2026-05-06).

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: Meterbox replaces fragmented monetization infrastructure with one programmable platform, built around a single immutable financial ledger. Every customer interaction becomes one financial event; everything else is projected from it. Instead of synchronizing systems, we derive different business views from one authoritative source — which reduces operational complexity while increasing financial correctness. Meterbox emphasizes customer data isolation, privacy by default, comprehensive auditability, strong authentication and access controls, flexible deployment for regulated or sovereign environments, and support for privacy and data-rights requirements. The platform is being built toward major enterprise security and compliance standards, while transparently documenting its current certifications, roadmap, security practices, third-party providers, accessibility efforts, and vulnerability-reporting processes.

Purpose-built for federal environments, NetCloud Federal provides a single cloud-delivered control plane to help agencies maintain reliable, compliant connectivity for mission-critical operations.

nonCertified.name: PostHog
nonCertified.useCase: Product analytics, session replay, and feature flags.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Browser and server clients supply analytics while the application reads feature flags from the PostHog control plane. For FedRAMP-enabled organizations, feature-flag requests carry the user identifier and, depending on the request, the email address and organization identifier or name, and no events or recordings. Except for one flag created in PostHog directly, flag existence and on/off state are managed in Pulumi and changed by pull request.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses PostHog to understand product usage and control staged feature delivery.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Analytics capture and session replay are disabled for FedRAMP-enabled organizations while feature-flag reads remain available.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: A per-organization FedRAMP setting blocks capture and recording for federal tenants. The setting is stored in the application database, not in PostHog, so no feature flag can turn it off.

nonCertified.name: SendGrid
nonCertified.useCase: Delivery of email a user writes and sends to a supplier (request for quote, purchase order, issue, supplier evaluation, and request for status), and delivery-event processing for those messages.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: SendGrid receives user-composed supplier email: the recipients, the subject and message the user writes, the request, order, issue, or evaluation details and share links Silkline adds, attached documents such as the purchase order PDF, and resource identifiers in delivery metadata. It sends signed delivery events to Silkline webhooks. System-generated email is sent through Amazon SES in AWS GovCloud over its FIPS endpoint.
nonCertified.justification: User-composed supplier email can be sent from the customer's own authenticated domain, which SendGrid domain authentication provides.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Only SendGridEmailService imports the SendGrid packages, enforced by a lint rule, and it accepts only the user-composed supplier email types, enforced by its type signature. Every system-generated email is sent through Amazon SES in AWS GovCloud.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: A user sends each message to recipients they choose, and the content they add is theirs under the shared responsibility model. Inbound delivery events require signature validation before processing.

nonCertified.name: Tailscale
nonCertified.useCase: Privileged network access and device coordination.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Tailscale is the administrative access path into the boundary, through bastions in AWS GovCloud. The coordination plane handles device identity, access policies, and connection metadata, and session payloads travel peer-to-peer and never reach it. Federal customer data does not reach Tailscale.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Tailscale to restrict administrative access to system resources.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: The Chief Technology Officer decided on 2026-09-23 to keep Tailscale as the administrative access path, outside the boundary, with bastions running Amazon Linux 2023 in FIPS mode. The use of WireGuard, which has no validated implementation, is a cryptographic departure the Chief Technology Officer accepted on 2026-10-20.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Every session inside the tailnet uses TLS through validated modules. Enforced tailnet access policies and Google Workspace sign-in restrict who can connect, and configuration and network flow logs stream to Datadog for Government.

nonCertified.name: Consolidated Screening List API
nonCertified.provider: International Trade Administration, U.S. Department of Commerce
nonCertified.useCase: Supplier screening against U.S. government restricted-party lists.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: When a user runs a supplier screen, Silkline sends the supplier name and the country of the supplier's primary address to data.trade.gov and stores the matches as an organization-scoped screening record.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses the Consolidated Screening List to support export compliance checks on suppliers.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Screens run only when a user starts one, and send no contacts, street addresses, or procurement details.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: The service is operated by a U.S. government agency, and requests use HTTPS with a subscription key held in Pulumi config.

nonCertified.name: Pulumi Cloud
nonCertified.useCase: Infrastructure state and deployment orchestration.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Pulumi Cloud stores infrastructure state and configuration environments and schedules deployments. Deployments of in-boundary stacks run on Silkline-managed runners in AWS GovCloud, except the two stacks that define those runners, which run on Pulumi-hosted runners. Federal customer data is not stored in Pulumi Cloud.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Pulumi Cloud for reproducible infrastructure management and deployment controls.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: The Chief Technology Officer decided on 2026-09-08 that Pulumi Cloud is a third-party resource outside the boundary, acting as the control plane for runners inside it. In-boundary stack secrets are encrypted with Silkline-managed KMS keys in AWS GovCloud, so Pulumi Cloud stores them only as ciphertext. Configuration environments, which hold production credentials, are encrypted at rest with a Silkline-managed key that Pulumi Cloud decrypts through a dedicated role when an environment opens.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: The fleet deploy role trusts Pulumi OIDC tokens from Silkline's organization and can be assumed only through the runners' STS endpoint. The two stacks that define the runners use a separate role that trusts only their own projects. A permissions boundary on every deploy role denies edits to deploy identities and reads of customer files in S3. CloudTrail records every use of the keys and roles, and revoking the environment key's role cuts off Pulumi Cloud's access to environment secrets.

nonCertified.name: GitHub
nonCertified.useCase: Source control, code review, and repository automation.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: GitHub hosts source code, pull requests, repository configuration, and automation credentials.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses GitHub as the authoritative software-development collaboration platform.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Repository changes require controlled review and protected-branch workflows.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Branch protections, CODEOWNERS, access reviews, and required CI checks protect the software supply chain.

nonCertified.name: Depot
nonCertified.useCase: Managed CI runners and container image builds.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Ephemeral Depot runners receive source code and scoped build secrets; selected workflow artifacts are retained for seven days.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Depot to run CI workloads and accelerate container builds.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: CI workflows use ephemeral runners, short artifact retention, and scoped access to build inputs.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: OIDC supplies short-lived Pulumi access and repository controls require reviewed changes before deployment.

nonCertified.name: Google Workspace
nonCertified.useCase: Corporate email, identity, documents, and collaboration.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Google Workspace provides staff email, groups, shared documents, and identity services used in company operations.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Google Workspace for workforce communication and collaboration.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Staff limit customer content in collaboration tools and use application workflows for operational records.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Central identity controls, multifactor authentication, and managed groups restrict workforce access.

nonCertified.name: Chainguard Images
nonCertified.useCase: FIPS-validated container base images.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Builds use Chainguard FIPS images pinned by digest and pulled through an Amazon ECR pull-through cache with a registry pull token.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Chainguard images to run FIPS-validated cryptography in its workloads.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Images are pinned by digest, and new pins arrive as reviewed pull requests.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: The pull credential has read-only scope, and cluster nodes cannot import images from the cache.

nonCertified.name: Plain
nonCertified.useCase: Customer support ticketing.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Plain stores support conversations and the customer contact details attached to them.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Plain to receive, track, and answer customer support requests.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Support staff limit customer content to what is needed to resolve the request.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: SSO with multifactor authentication restricts access to support staff.

nonCertified.name: ToDesktop
nonCertified.useCase: Desktop application builds, signing, and automatic updates.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: ToDesktop builds, signs, and distributes the Electron desktop application and its updates to user devices. The application loads app.silkline.ai and bundles only its shell, so federal customer data does not reach ToDesktop.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses ToDesktop to operate the desktop distribution and update channel.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: The Chief Technology Officer decided on 2026-10-20 that ToDesktop is a third-party resource outside the boundary. macOS builds are signed with Silkline's Developer ID and notarized by Apple, and Windows installers carry an Authenticode signature issued to Silkline, Inc.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: The application installs an update only when its signature matches Silkline's: the Apple team identifier on macOS and the Silkline, Inc. publisher on Windows. A release that the release workflow could not have built raises an alert to the engineering team.

nonCertified.name: Open Exchange Rates
nonCertified.useCase: Daily historical currency exchange rates.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: A scheduled task requests the rate table for each missing day and stores it as global reference data. Requests carry only a date and the application ID.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Open Exchange Rates to convert prices between currencies.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Requests contain no organization or customer data, and rates are stored once for all organizations.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: Requests use HTTPS and an application ID held in Pulumi ESC.

nonCertified.name: Merge
nonCertified.useCase: HRIS integration for employee and workforce data.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Organizations without FedRAMP enabled may connect an HRIS through Merge. Background tasks read employee names, email addresses, phone numbers, job titles, and reporting lines to provision users, and Merge sends webhooks when that data changes.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Merge to normalize supported human-resources systems.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: The HRIS integration is not available to FedRAMP-enabled organizations: they cannot create, enable, connect, or sync it.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: The refusal is enforced server-side. Database permissions reject an HRIS integration for a FedRAMP-enabled organization, and one organization-level gate runs before every sync and every Merge API call, including for an organization that enables FedRAMP after connecting.

nonCertified.name: Kernel
nonCertified.useCase: Managed browser sessions for desktop punchout workflows.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Kernel runs cloud browser sessions that can observe merchant content, session state, and credentials during desktop punchout.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Kernel to provide browser automation for desktop punchout.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Kernel-backed punchout and supplier sign-in are disabled for FedRAMP-enabled and ITAR organizations.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: One organization-level gate runs before every Kernel call and prevents federal sessions from starting in Kernel.

nonCertified.name: Context.dev
nonCertified.useCase: Enrichment of supplier and contact records.
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Background tasks run for organizations without FedRAMP enabled, when a supplier or contact is created or its domain or email changes. Lookups send the contact email, or the contact name with the linked company name and domain, and the supplier domain, or the supplier name when no domain is set. They receive public brand and professional profile data. Returned logos and profile photos are downloaded once and stored in Silkline storage, which the application serves them from.
nonCertified.justification: Silkline uses Context.dev to complete supplier brand and contact profiles without manual data entry.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Supplier and contact enrichment is disabled for FedRAMP-enabled organizations. Lookups send business identifiers only: work email addresses are lookup keys, personal-domain addresses such as Gmail are not. Low-confidence matches are discarded, and results fill only empty fields.
nonCertified.compensatingControls: One organization-level gate runs before every Context.dev call. Requests use HTTPS and an API key held in Pulumi ESC.

serviceIdentification.serviceName: Knox Systems FedRAMP High Managed Platform
serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Knox Systems gives commercial software companies a faster, simpler path to federal customers. Instead of pursuing a standalone FedRAMP authorization, application providers deploy into Knox's FedRAMP High authorized boundary and inherit a substantial share of the required security controls. Knox's compliance team and the KnoxAI platform guide each provider through readiness, assessment, and go-live. After go-live, Knox carries the ongoing compliance work and the security of the boundary, so providers can focus on their product and their agency customers.

Every application runs in its own dedicated, single-tenant account within the Knox authorization boundary, with no shared compute, data plane, or storage between customers. Each application is individually assessed, listed on the FedRAMP Marketplace, and covered by continuous monitoring from day one. All workloads run exclusively in US regions of AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud Platform with FIPS-validated encryption in transit and at rest. Access to the boundary follows a zero-trust model with full audit logging. Knox provides 24/7 Security Operations Center and Network Operations Center coverage, managed detection and response, continuous vulnerability and configuration scanning, and incident response for all hosted applications.

Knox is directly accountable for the compliance posture of the boundary. Knox manages continuous monitoring with monthly reporting to authorizing agencies, POA&M tracking, annual independent third-party assessments and penetration testing, and contingency and incident response exercises with every customer. A Shared Responsibility Matrix documents what Knox, the application provider, and the agency each own, so there is never ambiguity about who owns what.

KnoxAI is Knox Systems' FedRAMP authorization readiness and continuous monitoring platform. It turns months of manual authorization work into a simplified, guided process. KnoxAI handles the heavy lifting: it evaluates a customer's security posture and control implementation against NIST 800-53 and additional frameworks, shows where gaps exist and how to remediate them, and produces the artifacts FedRAMP requires. After go-live, KnoxAI helps customers stay compliant as their environment changes, catching new risks early and keeping remediation on track with FedRAMP timelines.

The following cloud service offerings are delivered within the Knox authorization boundary, each in its own dedicated single-tenant environment and each covered by the continuous monitoring program described above:

Adobe Connect is designed for immersive synchronous online meeting experiences for training, large-scale webinars, and virtual classroom meetings for a distributed workforce.

Backupta is a Resilience Platform for Okta that ensures uninterrupted identity and access management. It delivers secure backup, disaster recovery, and rapid restoration of tenants or objects. Tenant cloning and failover strengthen business continuity, while proactive monitoring and audit logs enhance security.

Peregrine enables public safety and government agencies to integrate, model, and access data from agency and authorized partner systems within a unified platform, allowing information about people, places, and events to be understood in context across systems. Peregrine supports workflows such as search, analysis, reporting, alerting, relationship mapping, and operational monitoring by providing a secure, continuously updated, permission-aware view of agency data for authorized users.

Sift is a SaaS platform for time-series telemetry ingestion, storage, visualization, and rule-based monitoring of mission-critical hardware systems. It serves mission operators, test engineers, and data analysts across federal agencies and their defense and aerospace contractors, providing interactive dashboards and programmatic query access to machine telemetry and associated operational metadata.

Altana Product Network (APN) is a SaaS offering in AWS GovCloud that uses artificial intelligence to create a single source of truth for the global supply chain. It integrates customer and external datasets to map suppliers, shipments, compliance, and risk, and is used by customer administrators and end users through a web portal with SAML 2.0 federation. The boundary is supported by EKS-based microservices, Databricks data pipelines, and core AWS services such as RDS, S3, OpenSearch, and ElastiCache.

Sierra is a multi-tenant SaaS Cloud Service Offering (CSO) that enables Federal agencies to build, deploy, and operate conversational AI agents that interact with the agency's constituents and employees across chat, voice, email, and other channels primarily to handle customer support, case intake, benefits inquiries, and similar service workflows autonomously so agencies can resolve high-volume citizen interactions at scale economically.

The Acsense IAM Resilience Platform is a cloud-based SaaS solution that serves as an Identity Control Plane, providing unified backup & recovery, disaster recovery on a separate remote tenant, configuration management, and compliance assurance capabilities for enterprise identity and access management (IAM) environments. The platform is IDP-agnostic by design, primarily supporting both Okta (Workforce and CIAM) and Microsoft Entra ID deployments.The system enables authorized administrators to back up enterprise identity infrastructure (including human and non-human identities/machine identities), track and compare configuration changes with full role attribution, map dependencies, detect configuration drift in approximately 10 minutes, and leverage Continuous Resilience Validation to ensure a tested ~10-minute Recovery Time Objective (RTO) during operational incidents, ransomware attacks, or outages. The authorization boundary includes the Acsense SaaS application, supporting management services, application APIs, data processing services, and storage components operated in cloud infrastructure environments. The platform is used by enterprise and government administrators, security teams, and IT operations personnel to process identity-related business data and limited personally identifiable information (PII) associated with IAM objects and user accounts. The service is delivered as a multi-tenant SaaS platform with customer-isolated data storage (or as a single, separated tenant) and relies on external identity provider APIs and cloud infrastructure services to perform authorized backup, synchronization, monitoring, and recovery operations.

Swimlane's Turbine is a multi-tenant SaaS agentic AI security automation platform which uses low-code technology to unify disparate cybersecurity tools into a centralized system of action. By utilizing agentic AI (Hero AI) alongside a visual, drag-and-drop playbook builder, the platform automates complex Security Operations Center (SOC) workflows, vulnerability management, and incident triage without requiring extensive custom coding. This comprehensive AI SOC orchestration eliminates alert fatigue for security teams, tracks compliance, and provides real-time ROI reporting to accelerate threat responses and protect large organizations globally.

Determinate is an SDLC collaboration and deployment automation platform. It specifically caters to the Nix ecosystem for reproducible and declarative software projects. Determinate processes and delivers software source code (FlakeHub, a source artifact repository) and compiled artifacts (FlakeHub Cache, a binary artifact repository) to end users as multi-tenant SaaS. Users publish their software via the customer's coding forge, like GitHub or GitLab.

The Vannevar platform supports government agencies and other authorized government users by running guided, agent-assisted workflows across disparate datasets and proprietary data to reduce the time required to turn raw information into investigative outputs. Within the platform, users can ingest and analyze digital artifacts and other government-provided data, correlate and search across those sources, and leverage agents to generate consistent work products. These workflows enable digital forensic sensemaking, investigative development and enrichment, and the production of shareable products for downstream action.

Tractian is an asset health monitoring platform that gives government agencies the intelligence to keep critical physical assets running in support of mission readiness, with security and compliance built for U.S. federal requirements. Wireless sensors and AI analytics support the whole asset health lifecycle, detecting developing failures, tracking how they progress, and guiding teams through to resolution before an issue becomes downtime or a safety event. The platform is deployed within Knox's FedRAMP High Authorized environment on AWS GovCloud, and it helps agencies and contractors get more output and reliability from the equipment they already have, without adding headcount, capital expense, or new risk.

MissionML Studio is a platform used to build, prototype, and productionize AI-enabled government workflow applications and securely host and monitor them. It is deployed as a secure, fully managed, single-tenant cloud platform where government program managers build and prototype custom AI workflow applications tailored to their mission needs and process operational, analytical, and mission data, while ensuring isolation for each customer environment.

Vectra AI delivers AI-native security and observability that helps federal security teams build and demonstrate resilience against modern cyber threats. The platform provides unified observability across on-premises networks, identity, cloud, SaaS, IoT/OT, edge, and AI infrastructure to identify active threats, prioritize investigation and response, and help agencies proactively reduce cyber risk and strengthen security posture. Federal security analysts, incident responders, administrators, and security leaders use the platform to monitor activity, investigate suspicious behavior, hunt for threats, contain compromised identities or devices, and assess gaps in security coverage. The platform provides contextual investigation, natural-language assistance, attack-path visualization, operational reporting, and evidence that supports continuous monitoring, compliance, and SOC optimization. More than 2,000 organizations use Vectra AI, which was named a Leader in the 2025 and 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Network Detection and Response.

Upwind Security is a SaaS cloud security platform that enables authorized users to identify and manage cloud vulnerabilities, security misconfigurations, runtime threats, and cloud asset inventory within cloud environments. The authorization boundary includes the Upwind application and supporting services necessary to provide these capabilities, processes cloud infrastructure metadata and security telemetry, and relies on AWS GovCloud (US) infrastructure and authorized external service dependencies to deliver the service.

SimpliGov is a cloud-based, multi-tenant Software-as-a-Service application that provides a government operations platform used by state and local agencies to design, run, and improve how their programs operate: digital forms that capture program data, and automation that moves applications, approvals, documents, signatures, and payments across teams and systems. The platform is used by more than 100 agencies and is sold only to U.S. public-sector customers.

The interos.ai Resilience Platform is a cloud-based, multi-tenant SaaS platform that delivers AI-powered supply chain risk intelligence to federal agencies, defense contractors, and commercial enterprises by ingesting, analyzing, and presenting supplier and business relationship data across six risk domains (Financial, Restrictions, Catastrophic, Geopolitical, ESG, and Cyber). Authorized users (procurement teams, risk managers, compliance officers) identify and monitor supply chain risks through web and API interfaces, configure custom risk rules and alert thresholds, and access risk intelligence.

Tranquility's TimePilot and HelioTrace are multi-tenant, SaaS-based platforms that support complex investigative and operational workflows across federal agencies. The platforms enable authorized personnel to securely ingest, organize, analyze, and synthesize large volumes of operational data using Super Intelligence-assisted natural language search, pattern recognition, automated work product generation, and standardized reporting to support informed decision-making. The services are hosted within a FedRAMP-authorized cloud environment and integrate with agency-provisioned data sources and approved operational systems.

BigID provides an automated foundation for data security, privacy, and governance across the federal enterprise. Delivered as SaaS on Amazon EKS in AWS GovCloud (US-East), the platform proactively discovers, classifies, and inventories sensitive data and AI assets across agency environments, including multi-cloud, on-premises data centers, and data pipelines, using a combination of techniques, including pattern matching and machine learning, to identify PII, PHI, and CUI. Agency administrators, privacy officers, security analysts, and data stewards use this visibility to mitigate risk, identify over-exposed data, revoke excessive access, and ensure regulatory compliance, with the resulting metadata, classifications, and catalog records stored in an in-cluster MongoDB database and Elastic Cloud.

SS&C Blue Prism WorkHQ is a multi-tenant SaaS enterprise automation and orchestration platform used by agency customers to design, deploy, run, and monitor automated work — including digital workers (RPA), human tasks, API integrations, and AI agents — from a single browser-based control plane. Within the authorization boundary, WorkHQ delivers the automation build environment (Design Studio), the asset and lifecycle service (Digital Worker Studio), the workflow and orchestration engine (Agentic Workflows), the AI governance layer (AI Gateway), and the shared identity, tenant, and audit services that support them. It is delivered as SaaS on AWS GovCloud (US), with logical tenant isolation between agency customers; the primary external dependency in scope for this listing is the underlying AWS GovCloud IaaS platform.

Wraithwatch is a SaaS cyber defense platform that gives federal security, compliance, and threat intelligence teams a single, real-time operating picture of their environment. AI agents autonomously build a data fabric and digital twin of the environment, including assets, connections, and attack paths, and continuously simulate how an adversary would move through it as it changes. Users query the twin in natural language, without vendor-specific query languages, for continuous ATO and control-drift tracking, cross-source threat hunting, and autonomous threat intelligence feeds, completing in minutes work that took days or weeks. Wraithwatch is currently in use across federal agencies and critical infrastructure organizations.

Harvey for Government allows attorneys and legal professionals at federal agencies to use AI across their legal work. Users can work through legal questions, review their agency's documents, draft and revise work product such as memos, briefs, and correspondence, run multi-step legal workflows, and collaborate on matters in shared workspaces, with responses that cite their sources. Harvey for Government helps agency legal teams spend less time on routine review and drafting and more time on higher-judgment work.

Arch Cloud is an agentic AI platform for manufacturing operations that ingests production data from existing factory systems (MES, ERP, SCADA, PLCs, sensors, and equipment automation), identifies the root causes of quality and performance issues, and delivers guided corrective actions to the operators, engineers, and site and global operations leaders who can act on them. The platform processes factory operational and time-series telemetry — error codes, cycle times, UPH, downtime events, CPK trends, OEE, and routing data across various manufacturing environments. It is delivered as a single-tenant cloud (SaaS) offering whose major components — the Arch Data Twin integration layer, Arch AI analytics, and Arch GLO guidance delivery — are powered by customers' existing factory infrastructure as the source of that data.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Game Warden is a fully managed and compliant multi-tenant DevSecOps platform that accelerates the delivery of commercial cloud software to federal government customers, State, Local, and Education (SLED) agencies, and highly regulated industries. Engineered to support dual compliance pathways, Game Warden can be leveraged as a pre-authorized FedRAMP PaaS for external systems or utilized for fully in-boundary application hosting. Built to provide Fort Knox-level infrastructure security, customer workloads deploy natively on our managed infrastructure across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) utilizing Kubernetes containers. The platform fully automates continuous monitoring, threat mitigation, vulnerability scanning, patch management, and control inheritance required to conform to strict cybersecurity standards across the full compliance spectrum—FedRAMP, DoW, and GovRAMP. Second Front Systems handles 100% of the underlying infrastructure maintenance, enabling commercial SaaS technology to rapidly scale across public sector and regulated missions without the overhead of building traditional compliance frameworks from scratch.

Akeyless is an identity security platform for machines, autonomous agents, and humans that unifies secrets management, privileged access, certificate lifecycle management, encryption keys and AI agent runtime controls on a Zero-Knowledge cryptographic foundation.

American Intelligence Corporation (AIC) provides an advanced AI infrastructure platform designed to automate complex systems integration, data processing, and operational workflows for mission-critical operations across public sector and defense agencies.

Clearview AI is a facial recognition intelligence platform featuring a database of billions of public web images. It empowers law enforcement and government agencies to rapidly identify suspects, generate investigative leads, and enhance public safety.

Cohere is an enterprise-grade AI platform that builds frontier large language models and semantic retrieval systems. It enables businesses to integrate advanced text generation, natural language processing, and AI search directly into secure applications.

DailyPay is a financial technology solution that seamlessly integrates with enterprise payroll software to give employees real-time, on-demand access to their earned wages, enhancing financial wellness and driving workforce retention for employers.

DataRobot is an enterprise AI platform designed to accelerate end-to-end machine learning. It automates the development, deployment, continuous monitoring, and governance of predictive analytics and generative AI applications at scale across businesses.

DataOS (by The Modern Data Company) is a data operating system that unifies, governs, and transforms fragmented enterprise data architectures into standardized, AI-ready data products without requiring the replacement of existing legacy infrastructure.

Dropzone AI is an Agentic SOC platform that deploys autonomous AI security analysts. Working alongside human teams, these agents investigate alerts across core security tools to deliver scalable threat coverage and detailed, verifiable evidence reports.

JetStream Security is an AI governance and security platform that offers deep visibility, identity access management, and real-time runtime guardrails, empowering enterprises to safely deploy, monitor, and control AI workflows and autonomous agents.

Kaizen Labs is a modern administrative cloud platform built specifically for local government agencies. It streamlines municipal operations by digitizing citizen services, online permitting, business licensing, and parks and recreation management workflows.

MCheck (by HiLabs) is an AI-driven healthcare data clearinghouse platform that automates complex provider data workflows. It eliminates errors, improves directory accuracy, streamlines roster ingestion, and optimizes operational efficiency for health plans.

Onebrief is a collaborative mission-planning platform that unifies real-time operational data, staff workflows, and decision intelligence into a single interface to accelerate command-and-control processes across defense and coalition operations.

Dayforce HCM, Public Sector (Dayforce Pub Sec) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) Human Capital Management (HCM) cloud service offering deployed in a public cloud environment for use by U.S. Federal Government agencies. The service provides integrated capabilities for human resources, payroll, workforce management, benefits administration, document management, employee communications, analytics, reporting, and secure application integration through a single logical application platform.

The FedRAMP authorization boundary includes the Dayforce Pub Sec application services, management services, identity and access management services, document management services, integration services, messaging services, analytics services, and supporting cloud platform components required to deliver the service. Only those services, features, and components included within the authorization boundary have been independently assessed as part of the FedRAMP Moderate authorization.

The service supports federated identity using customer-managed identity providers and implements Digital Identity Level 2 (IAL2/AAL2) requirements, including multifactor authentication and identity federation, as applicable. The service employs role-based access control, privileged access management, centralized audit logging, continuous monitoring, vulnerability management, incident response, and FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules to protect federal information in transit and at rest.

Dayforce Pub Sec is designed to process, store, and transmit Federal Moderate impact information, including Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), in accordance with FIPS PUB 199 Moderate security requirements. Security responsibilities are shared between Dayforce and customer agencies as defined in the Customer Responsibility Matrix, with customer organizations responsible for agency-managed identity governance, endpoint security, and organization-specific security controls.

certified.useCase:
Resource Name: Amazon Web Services (AWS Commercial)
General Usage & Configuration: Cloud Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) and Platform as a Service (PaaS) configured using AWS Organizations, IAM Identity Center, isolated VPCs, and centralized encryption.
Justification for Use: Delivers scalable, highly available compute, storage, networking, and managed database services to host critical workloads.
Mitigation Measures: Implement AWS KMS encryption at rest and in transit, GuardDuty threat monitoring, CloudTrail audit logging, AWS WAF, and multi-factor authentication for all IAM identities.
Compensating Controls: AWS Control Tower posture guardrails, automated compliance drift evaluation via AWS Config, and mandatory egress filtering through centralized firewalls.

Resource Name: Paramify Cloud
General Usage & Configuration: Automated cybersecurity documentation and GRC platform configured to auto-generate and maintain OSCAL-based System Security Plans (SSPs) and compliance artifacts.
Justification for Use: Automates compliance documentation drafting for NIST SP 800-53 and FedRAMP baselines, reducing manual oversight and documentation drift.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce RBAC for platform access, mandate SSO/MFA for all users, enforce AES-256 encryption at rest for generated compliance files, and sanitize operational details.
Compensating Controls: Internal technical lead and CISO manual sign-off on all system boundaries, control implementations, and generated SSP artifacts before submission.

nonCertified.name: 1Password
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Enterprise credential vault and secret management configured with zero-knowledge encryption, enforced Master Password + Secret Key policies, mandatory MFA, and role-based vault segregation.
Justification for Use: Centralizes credential management, prevents plain-text secret storage, and eliminates risky password-reuse practices across administrative and operational teams.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce zero-knowledge architecture, continuous device trust validation, admin IP allowlisting, and automated secret rotation schedules.
Compensating Controls: Mandatory integration with primary Identity Provider (SSO) for automated user provisioning/deprovisioning; secret access auditing via SIEM ingestion.

nonCertified.name: 3rd Degree
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Pre-employment background verification and identity screening platform configured with encrypted candidate invite links and policy-driven adjudication workflows.
Justification for Use: Verifies candidate background, credentials, and legal eligibility to mitigate insider threat risks before granting access to corporate infrastructure.
Mitigation Measures: Limit PII exposure via strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), enforce TLS 1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest, enforce strict data retention schedules, and execute DPAs/BAAs.
Compensating Controls: HR and Legal double-check and sign off on screening results before access is granted; zero system access or account creation prior to background clearance.

nonCertified.name: A-LIGN
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Automated compliance management and audit portal (A-SCEND) configured for automated evidence collection, continuous control monitoring, and audit submission.
Justification for Use: Streamlines SOC 2, ISO 27001, and FedRAMP assessment workflows, centralizing audit artifacts and continuous posture evaluation.
Mitigation Measures: Restrict portal access to compliance staff via SSO/MFA, apply least-privilege read-only permissions to audit integrations, and scrub sensitive PII/PHI from uploaded artifacts.
Compensating Controls: Continuous manual review of all compliance evidence prior to auditor release; annual review of A-LIGN’s SOC 2 Type II assessment reports.

nonCertified.name: Atlassian (Confluence & Jira)
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Enterprise cloud documentation knowledge base and issue tracking configured with SAML 2.0 SSO, strict space/project permissions, and encrypted storage.
Justification for Use: Centralizes compliance policy management, technical documentation, and security ticket tracking across operational teams.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce OneLogin SSO with hardware-token MFA, restrict public space/project sharing, enforce IP allowlisting, and sanitize sensitive PII/PHI from wiki pages.
Compensating Controls: Mandatory SIEM log ingestion for admin activity; annual SOC 2 Type II review of Atlassian Cloud controls.

nonCertified.name: Google Workspace
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Cloud productivity, corporate email (Gmail), and document collaboration (Drive) configured with Client-Side Encryption (CSE), context-aware access controls, and strict DLP rules.
Justification for Use: Provides enterprise email, communication, and document sharing required for business operations.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce SSO with hardware-token MFA, implement strict Data Loss Prevention (DLP) rules blocking external sharing of sensitive data, and restrict OAuth app authorizations.
Compensating Controls: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) software on all enterprise devices; continuous automated email security gateway scanning to filter phishing attempts.

nonCertified.name: Ninjio
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Security awareness micro-learning and phishing simulation platform configured with automated monthly training modules and simulated phishing campaigns.
Justification for Use: Strengthens staff defense mechanisms against social engineering, phishing, and malware threats, ensuring compliance with federal awareness standards.
Mitigation Measures: Anonymize user profiles using minimal PII (email/pseudonym only) during account provisioning; enforce strict administrative SSO access.
Compensating Controls: Automated email security gateways (e.g., Defender for Office 365 / Proofpoint) that analyze, neutralize, and quarantine real-world threats independently of user action.

nonCertified.name: OneLogin
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Enterprise Identity and Access Management (IAM) and Single Sign-On (SSO) solution configured with Adaptive MFA, SAML 2.0/OIDC integrations, and automated SCIM provisioning.
Justification for Use: Centralizes user identity authentication, access enforcement, and automated user lifecycle management across all corporate SaaS and cloud systems.
Mitigation Measures: Require step-up Adaptive MFA based on risk scoring, enforce robust password complexity guidelines, limit session durations, and forward auth logs to a SIEM.
Compensating Controls: Secured break-glass administrative credentials maintained in offline physical vaults; baseline access policies for critical infrastructure when SSO is unreachable.

nonCertified.name: OpenVPN Server
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Centralized Virtual Private Network host application managing encrypted tunnel connections configured with TLS 1.3, AES-256-GCM, and client certificate authentication.
Justification for Use: Grants encrypted, authenticated remote access to private corporate networks and non-public cloud infrastructure for remote staff.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce multi-factor authentication alongside key-based client certificates, restrict split tunneling, enforce tight firewall rules on VPN gateways, and log session data.
Compensating Controls: Network-level micro-segmentation limiting VPN client routing exclusively to authorized IP ranges and application ports based on user role.

nonCertified.name: Terraform
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) tool configured to manage cloud resource provisioning, utilizing remote state locking and encrypted backend storage.
Justification for Use: Enables repeatable, version-controlled, and audited infrastructure deployments, reducing human configuration error.
Mitigation Measures: Encrypt state files at rest using KMS AES-256, restrict state file access strictly to CI/CD service accounts, scan code for secrets/misconfigurations prior to commit, and require peer code reviews.
Compensating Controls: Separation of duties preventing developers from directly applying infrastructure changes; all executions must run through isolated, audited CI/CD pipelines.

nonCertified.name: Twilio
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Cloud communications platform configured for programmatic SMS messaging, system status alerts, and multi-factor authentication token delivery via REST APIs.
Justification for Use: Enables automated application-to-person notifications, out-of-band verification codes, and real-time operational status alerts.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce strict TLS API communication, scope API tokens to minimum required capabilities, implement strict rate-limiting, and validate incoming webhooks via digital signatures.
Compensating Controls: Offer secondary/fallback out-of-band authentication methods (e.g., TOTP authenticator apps, WebAuthn push notifications) to mitigate SIM-swapping risks inherent to SMS.

nonCertified.name: Udemy Business
nonCertified.useCase:
General Usage & Configuration: Enterprise digital learning platform configured via SAML 2.0 SSO for user identity verification and automated LMS profile creation.
Justification for Use: Provides ongoing technical skill development, cybersecurity training courses, and professional development for staff.
Mitigation Measures: Enforce SSO/MFA authentication, restrict public course publishing from enterprise accounts, and minimize shared account details to essential attributes (Name/Work Email).
Compensating Controls: Corporate endpoint isolation and web filtering policies preventing personal web activity or file downloads from impacting enterprise networks.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
The Anomali Cloud Service Offering consists of two integrated components: Security Analytics and ThreatStream, delivered as a unified cloud-native security platform. Security Analytics provides AI and cloud-native security information and event management (SIEM) capabilities including data collection and normalization from network devices, endpoints, applications, and cloud services; real-time event correlation and threat detection using machine learning algorithms; behavioral analytics and anomaly detection; incident response workflows; and query capabilities across petabytes of historical data stored in an integrated security data lake with configurable retention periods up to 7+ years. The platform supports ingestion of 30TB+ of data within hours and enables sub-second query response times across petabyte-scale datasets using natural language processing and AI-supported interfaces.

ThreatStream provides threat intelligence management capabilities including automated collection, normalization, and curation of threat intelligence from commercial feeds, open source intelligence, and information sharing centers; management of indicators of compromise (IOCs) and indicators of attack (IOAs) with automated deduplication and confidence scoring; correlation of external threat intelligence with internal security telemetry; distribution of actionable intelligence to integrated security tools via APIs and standard protocols; threat analysis and enrichment with MITRE ATT&CK framework mapping; and secure community-based threat sharing. The service operates as a multi-tenant Software-as-a-Service solution with role-based access controls, data encryption in transit and at rest, comprehensive audit logging, and RESTful APIs for integration with existing security infrastructure. Service boundaries include all data ingestion interfaces, processing engines, storage systems, user interfaces, APIs, and integration points necessary to deliver security analytics and threat intelligence management capabilities.

The Collaborative Learning Environment (CLE) is a full-featured, end-to-end virtual school platform for managing learning, providing brick-and-mortar-like classroom experiences using audio, video, live collaboration tools and asynchronous tools and LMS capabilities.
System capabilities include:
- Real-time collaboration with audio, video, shared content, and recording capabilities
- User management
- Reporting and data analysis
- Classroom management including assignments, evaluations, and grading
- Central repository for media and other shared materials with the ability to build and edit course materials from a single workspace

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: VulcanGov (Justinian for Government) is a SaaS AI platform for government: an AI agent workspace grounded in a curated, continuously updated library of federal and state statutes, regulations, guidance and housing datasets, with full-text and semantic search, secure single-use agent sandboxes for code execution and document generation, and an administration console for agency user management, session audit visibility and usage export. It is delivered from a government-only environment in AWS GovCloud (US) (us-gov-east-1) on a containerized microservices architecture: AWS ECS Fargate, Aurora PostgreSQL, S3 object storage, OpenSearch and ElastiCache. Federal customer data is stored in AWS GovCloud (US). Large language model inference runs in Amazon Bedrock in commercial AWS regions (us-east-1, us-east-2 and us-west-2), reached over a documented transport bridge: prompts and the content supplied with them are processed there. Every cross-boundary resource, including any temporary deviation, is disclosed in the published third-party information resources and service-scope lists rather than omitted. Data is encrypted at rest (AWS KMS, AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) with FIPS 140-validated cryptographic modules; identity and access are federated through Okta for Government with enforced multi-factor authentication; security monitoring uses Datadog for Government, Wiz for Government and native AWS security services. Available to federal, state and local governments and to organizations working on their behalf. Public offering information, the secure configuration guide and live availability status are published on the Trust Center at https://trust.vulcangov.app; FedRAMP Certification Data is available to federal reviewers through its gated portal.

TrackVia brings workflows, data, automation, mobile capabilities, integrations, and AI together in a secure, governed platform.

TrackVia supports use cases including field operations, inspections, workforce and mission readiness, asset and equipment management, safety and compliance, program operations, contractor and vendor management, and other mission critical workflows.

**Remedio: correction beats visibility. Find it, fix it, prove it — at machine speed.**

Remedio is a configuration-focused device hardening and autonomous remediation offering that finds, fixes, and verifies security misconfigurations, unpatched vulnerabilities, unauthorized applications, and unmanaged AI tools across agency endpoints and servers, wherever they run — on premises, remote, or in the cloud. Hardening continues off-network, indefinitely.

Remedio closes the loop between detection and correction by applying policy-controlled, automated fixes and giving administrators an instant, auditable rollback path for every change. This lets government security teams enforce baselines like DISA STIG, NIST 800-53, and CIS Benchmarks continuously — not just at audit time — while reducing the manual workload historically required to close configuration and compliance gaps at scale.

**Core capabilities**

1. **Remedio Baseline — configuration hardening.** Establishes and continuously enforces secure configuration baselines (Golden Images) across Windows, Linux, and macOS endpoints and servers, automatically correcting drift as it occurs.
2. **Remedio Fortify — vulnerability and misconfiguration remediation.** Identifies and prioritizes vulnerabilities and misconfigurations, then applies safe, automated remediation at scale to reduce patch and hardening backlogs.
3. **Remedio Assure — continuous compliance.** Continuously validates configuration and remediation state against required control frameworks and agency-specific policy, maintaining audit-ready evidence and full traceability for oversight and reporting.
4. **Remedio Gate — application control.** Discovers and controls installed software, scripts, and services, blocking unauthorized or risky applications, browser plugins, and dev-tool extensions before they create exposure.
5. **Remedio AI Govern — shadow AI governance.** Discovers and governs AI tools, models, agents, and connected integrations in use across the environment, bringing shadow AI into visibility and enforcing approved-use policy and access controls.

**How it works**

Each Remedio capability operates on a continuous cycle: **Review** (aggregate device state against secure baselines), **Reveal** (surface misconfigurations, identity gaps, and shadow AI usage), **Reassess** (ongoing validation against baselines and compliance mandates), **Remediate** (apply policy-controlled fixes, closing findings as they are detected rather than waiting on manual ticket cycles), and **Revert** (instant rollback of any change if conditions require). The cycle runs on the device itself, so scanning and remediation continue while a device is off the network, and findings upload when it reconnects. Every remediation action is logged for audit and reporting purposes, and the platform includes built-in ROI reporting to quantify time saved, risk reduced, and compliance gains.

Live evidence: [Trust Center](https://trust.remedio.io) · [Secure Configuration Guide](https://trust.remedio.io/scg) · [Certification progress](https://trust.remedio.io/progress) · [remedio.io](https://remedio.io)

Cloudflare operates a global network that delivers security, performance, and reliability from a single platform. Cloudflare for Government provides this same platform to U.S. Government agencies as one homogeneous stack. This Marketplace listing consolidates both of Cloudflare for Government's FedRAMP Certifications — Class C (previously FedRAMP Moderate) and Class D (previously FedRAMP High) — into a single product entry. The certified services span:

- **SASE / Zero Trust** — Zero Trust network access, secure web gateway, CASB, browser isolation, data loss prevention, email security, and cloud-delivered WAN.
- **Security** — web application firewall (WAF), DDoS protection, API security, bot management, rate limiting, and client-side security.
- **Network & Content Delivery** — CDN, authoritative DNS, load balancing, smart routing, and network interconnect.
- **Compute** — serverless functions, containers, durable objects, and workflow orchestration.
- **Storage** — object storage, SQL and key-value databases, and queues.

Federal agencies use Cloudflare to protect public-facing websites and APIs, secure workforce access to internal applications, replace legacy remote-access VPN and MPLS connectivity, and build cloud-native applications entirely within the FedRAMP-certified boundary.

The two Certifications are delivered from separate environments with separate control planes. Class C is accessed at dash.cloudflare.com and api.cloudflare.com; Class D is accessed at dash.fed.cloudflare.com and api.fed.cloudflare.com. Federal customers select the environment that matches the FedRAMP Certification required for their workload.

This offering is FedRAMP Class C and Class D Certified. The scope of the two Certifications differs by a small number of services; per-service class is denoted in the Certified Services list as follows: services with no notation are Certified at both Class C and Class D, services marked with an asterisk (*) are Certified at Class C only (not within the Class D boundary), and services marked with a dagger (†) are Certified at Class D only (not within the Class C boundary). Learn more at https://www.cloudflare.com/public-sector/

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Constellation GovCloud (CGC) is an information system that provides the necessary Platform as a Service (PaaS) architecture layers to support Merlin-operated Software as a Service (SaaS) applications. These Merlin SaaS applications will be hosted and provided to U.S. federal agencies, including local and state governments and tribal organizations. The CGC is part of a managed service that is designed to accelerate FedRAMP authorizations allowing Merlin SaaS companies to achieve a FedRAMP Authority to Operate (ATO) more quickly and cost-effectively.

**Services undergoing approval for use — not authorized.** The following services are hosted on CGC but are **not** authorized services and are **not** included in this certification. They are undergoing approval for use and are recorded here for transparency only; none is covered by this package, and each moves into the certified service list only on completion of that approval.

- **QIZ** — QIZ delivers a cloud-based cryptography posture management platform for government agencies and regulated organizations to manage cryptographic risk. The system provides centralized capabilities for cryptographic discovery and inventory, correlation of findings to affected systems and owners, policy definition, risk-based triage, root cause analysis, and remediation planning. QIZ collects cryptographic data from network traffic, system and application configurations, source code, binaries, and cloud infrastructure. Cryptographic standards are defined within the platform, and the system evaluates the environment against those standards to report current posture and identify policy violations. QIZ produces a contextualized cryptographic bill of materials (CBOM), exportable in standard formats, and a policy driven transition plan prioritized by risk and business context, giving agencies a sequenced and repeatable path toward post-quantum readiness.

- **Veeam** — Veeam Data Cloud Gov for Microsoft 365 is a fully managed Software as a Service (SaaS) backup solution for federal, state, and local government agencies that need to protect and recover their Microsoft 365 data. The service runs on Microsoft Azure within Constellation GovCloud's boundary and backs up Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and OneDrive. Backups stay immutable, so they cannot be altered or deleted, even from a compromised administrator account. Agencies sign in through their own identity provider and use role-based access control to decide who can manage and restore data. When ransomware, a compromised account, or a large-scale data loss strikes, agencies can quickly restore what they need and limit disruption to mission-critical services. Built on a native integration with Microsoft 365 Backup Storage, the service enables fast initial backup with no API throttling, delivering restore performance at speeds exceeding 1TB per hour. There is no infrastructure for agencies to manage, and storage is included with per-user licensing.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription: Cynamics, a leading innovator in network cybersecurity, presents a next-generation SOC AI platform powered by its proprietary sample-based NDR and cybersecurity large language model, CynLLM. By integrating intelligent sampling with cutting-edge AI, Cynamics facilitates real-time and scalable threat detection without the heavy infrastructure requirements of traditional solutions. Already endorsed by Tier-1 municipalities, enterprises, and critical infrastructure providers globally, Cynamics offers unparalleled visibility, automation, and operational efficiency for today's security teams.

Hyperproof delivers a modern, cloud-based compliance operations platform designed to help government agencies and regulated organizations manage risk and compliance with confidence. Hyperproof Gov is a cloud-based governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platform designed to support regulated organizations in managing security and compliance programs. The system provides centralized capabilities for control management, evidence collection, risk tracking, audit support, and continuous monitoring. Hyperproof Gov enables structured workflows and real-time compliance status reporting to support authorization, assessment, and ongoing monitoring activities. The platform is designed to integrate with external systems for automated evidence collection and to maintain traceability between controls, requirements, and supporting artifacts, supporting consistent and repeatable compliance operations.

InfoSec Global Federal's AgileSec Analytics provides automated discovery, monitoring, and policy-driven control of cryptographic assets, including keys, certificates, algorithms, libraries, devices, applications, firmware, and protocols, across cloud and on-premise environments. The AgileSec Analytics platform ensures agencies are prepared for emerging cryptographic threats, including quantum attacks, by monitoring usage of cryptography and preparing migration to post-quantum cryptography. Key capabilities include Automated Cryptographic Discovery & Inventory, Vulnerability Identification and Compliance Reporting, Post-Quantum Readiness, and Continuous Monitoring and Remediation Workflows. The AgileSec Analytics solution supports regulatory requirements including OMB 23-02 mandates and continuous diagnostics, with built-in reporting features evaluated and recognized by federal standards organizations. It also integrates with numerous ecosystem technologies including EDR, CLM, PKI, HSM, CDM dashboards, ITSM, GRC tools and more.

Torq combines agentic insights and automation so that federal agencies and public sector organizations can triage, investigate, and respond to actual risks, faster. Torq streamlines every step from alert through resolution, expanding capacity and throughput. First, Torq ingests and normalizes telemetry from across your security stack, preparing the data for agentic reasoning at scale. Auto Triage filters out noise and prioritizes actual threats. Next, cases are automatically opened and assigned to highly specialized AI agents designed for investigation and response. Using tools and actions you specify, they gather evidence, assemble timelines, and transparently record decisions and authorized actions. Your team is in complete control. With Torq, your SOC delivers more results, more efficiently, from triage through remediation.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: Cohesity helps public sector agencies strengthen cyber resilience through a compliance-focused portfolio of cloud data protection and recovery services. Cohesity Cloud Services for Government brings together secure backup, rapid recovery, centralized management, and cyber vaulting in a streamlined service experience, helping agencies reduce operational complexity, protect mission-critical data, and recover with confidence from ransomware and other disruptive events. The portfolio includes Cohesity DataProtect and Helios for Government capabilities, as well as FortKnox SaaS vaults for DataProtect. FortKnox provides Cohesity-managed cyber vaulting that helps isolate backup data from production environments, with cold- and warm-tier vaulting options, anomaly-detection reporting, and flexible recovery capabilities. Together, these offerings give public sector agencies a scalable way to modernize data protection, improve resilience, and support mission continuity.

Core capabilities: (1) automated, authorized penetration testing and adversary emulation against customer-designated in-scope targets; (2) asset discovery and inventory with vulnerability aggregation and risk scoring; (3) governance, risk, and compliance monitoring that maps findings and evidence to frameworks such as NIST SP 800-53, PCI DSS, HIPAA, CIS Controls, and SOC 2 and reports control gaps with remediation guidance; and (4) security reporting and dashboards. An optional lightweight TNT endpoint sensor forwards host security telemetry to the platform's cloud analysis services for continuous analysis and threat hunting. The TNT Business Resilience Platform also integrates Agger ransomware protection capabilities, including endpoint-based behavioral detection, prevention, and response. Applicable cloud services supporting these capabilities are incorporated into the TNT service architecture and FedRAMP assessment scope. Automated assessment and analysis are performed by AI agents operating under human supervision.

Cisco Cloud Control with AgenticOps
Cisco Cloud Control with AgenticOps serves as the autonomous control plane for hybrid cloud environments. By integrating "AgenticOps"—a framework of specialized, task-oriented AI agents—the system moves beyond traditional automation into autonomous remediation and lifecycle management. It is designed to handle complex compliance requirements by enabling agents to autonomously detect drift, perform vulnerability remediation, and ensure that infrastructure state remains continuously aligned with defined security policies.

Cisco Cloud Control is the unified management and orchestration platform for hybrid and multi-cloud environments. It acts as the central plane for governing, securing, and operating distributed infrastructure, providing consistent policy enforcement and lifecycle automation across disparate cloud services and data centers. By centralizing management, it eliminates operational silos, streamlines compliance, and ensures that infrastructure remains performant and secure at scale.
The Rich Suite of Offers
To support the autonomous capabilities of Cloud Control, the following products integrate into a cohesive operational ecosystem:
1. AI Canvas
Description: The design and orchestration workbench for the AgenticOps ecosystem. AI Canvas provides a visual interface for engineering teams to design, model, and deploy autonomous agents. It allows for the mapping of complex operational workflows into executable logic, ensuring that agents are constrained by well-defined operational boundaries before they are deployed to manage production environments.
2. AI Assistant
Description: The natural language operational interface for the suite. AI Assistant bridges the gap between human intent and machine execution. It enables engineers to query system status, request complex remediation tasks, or gain insights into compliance posture through conversational interactions. It serves as the primary gateway for users to interface with the autonomous agents created in AI Canvas.
3. AI Defense
Description: The dedicated security layer for the AI model pipeline and agentic infrastructure. AI Defense provides the necessary guardrails to protect AI models from adversarial manipulation, data leakage, and unauthorized access. In high-compliance environments, it ensures that the models driving the agents are hardened, verifiable, and protected against vulnerabilities that could compromise the integrity of the automated security remediation processes.

Designed for agencies with up to 80,000 unified communications endpoints and 24,000 knowledge workers or agents, it allows you to scale as needed to meet citizen demand.
 
By applying technologies like journey orchestration, analytics, and AI/automation you can deliver efficient and intuitive constituent services while reducing overall contact center costs.
 
Key Features
 
Experience Cloud integrates with Humanify Enterprise Workforce Optimization SaaS (WFOaaS Quality Assurance / Call Recording / Desktop Screen Recording, Speech Analytics, and Post Call IVR surveys, powered by Verint) to enable departments and agencies to capture citizen and stakeholder feedback after interactions with contact center agents, and then utilize that input to drive coaching and feedback. TTEC Humanify Enterprise - Government platform users can now obtain the unique value of these solutions working together to drive improvements in citizen and stakeholder service.
 
WFOaaS Quality Assurance / Call Recording / Desktop Screen Recording. The Humanify Enterprise Workforce Optimization Software as a Service for Government Community Cloud provides Quality Monitoring (QM), Contact Recording, Text to Speech Analytics. The service records 100% of voice calls and 15% of contact center agent desktop screen recordings for compliance, transaction verification, and legal protection. Data is stored in a FedRAMP encrypted format and available for playback and analysis and for agent performance scoring.

Workforce Management (WFM) provides forecasting, multi-skill scheduling, and real-time adherence for contact center agents. Includes features for workflows, intra-day dynamic scheduling, audit trail reporting, and mentoring requests.
The speech-enabled Interactive Voice Response (IVR) enhanced by Natural Language Processing and Natural Language Understanding (NLU/NLP) enables seamless self-service capability through the use of Voice Bot and Chat Bot capability.
 
Experience Cloud, powered by Verint Experience Management Experience Cloud, is a SaaS application platform that utilizes the TTEC Humanify Enterprise - G to make delivering exceptional experiences easy. The Experience Cloud gathers omni-channel experience information from citizens, employees, and digital site visitors and helps to prioritize and provide key insights on ways to improve those experiences. 
 
Process and analyze direct feedback from multi-channel surveys, unstructured text data from open-ends and other comment streams, and behavior data from web interactions
Automate and speed decision-making with our proprietary Predictive Engine paired with Verint Professional Services guidance 
Operationalize across all functions with real-time triggers and alerts; custom dashboards for executives, service center managers, and contact center managers and agents; and case management tools for follow-ups when appropriate with a citizen or other key stakeholders
 
Experience Cloud consists of multiple solutions that work either singly or together to capture, analyze, and act on citizen and stakeholder feedback. These solutions include:
 
Predictive Experience allows organizations to measure citizen experiences across channels, prioritize resources effectively, accurately benchmark performance, and bring certainty to their experience programs with proven predictive data science and AI-powered technologies. 
Digital Experience captures real-time citizen-initiated feedback via web and mobile channels throughout the digital citizen journey, empowering organizations to make smarter, faster decisions to improve experiences.
Enterprise Experience enables organizations to engage citizens and employees to understand, analyze, and orchestrate improved experiences, satisfaction, and trust across multiple channels.
Text Analytics provides the ability to analyze text information from any text stream, including surveys, comment posts, and others, and to extract key insights found in those text comments around the topics, keywords, and the related sentiment expressed in those comments 
Unified Experience enables Federal departments and agencies to capture feedback across virtually any channel, combine those feedback channels (and a wide variety of external data sources to enrich the data, correlate the information from disparate sources to create customized data models, and then use those data models to drive collaboration and closed-loop action on the data.
 
Humanify Portal provides easy access to your contact center and unified communications administrative and management tools from a single interface. It increases the flexibility of the platform. It allows end-user administrators to perform Move, Add, Change, and Delete (MACD) activities for phones, personnel, locations, skill groups, agent teams, and many other system elements. It also allows administrators to change routing rules, IVR prompts, call queues, and contact flows. You can also increase the agility of managing your contact center operations with Humanify Portal Mobile, a 100% web-based application for on-the-move access. (508 Compliant)
 
Integration with Contact Center Solutions (Cisco, Genesys, and Amazon Connect)
 
Availability and Support
 
High availability/disaster recovery deployed across two data centers for full failover in the event of an outage
24x7x365 support with one of the largest pools of Cisco-certified engineers anywhere
