serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
DigiCert for U.S. Government helps federal agencies reduce certificate-related outages gain control over the digital identities, certificates, cryptographic keys, and software their systems depend on. The unified SaaS platform gives teams a consistent way to manage these risks across their users, devices, workloads, and applications.

Through  DigiCert® ONE  on AWS GovCloud (US), the platform helps agencies discover and automate certificate lifecycles, operate private certificate authorities, protect software-signing processes and supply chains, and enforce consistent administrative access controls. These integrated capabilities help agencies reduce certificate-related outages, strengthen cyber resilience, improve auditability, and manage digital trust across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments.

DigiCert for U.S. Government includes three integrated solutions:

•	DigiCert® Trust Lifecycle Manager:
CA-agnostic certificate lifecycle management (CLM) solution providing centralized discovery, inventory, enrollment, and automated renewal of public and private certificates across users, devices, servers, and infrastructure, eliminating manual tracking and reducing certificate-related outages. It supports standard enrollment protocols (ACME, EST, SCEP, and CMP) and integrates natively with AWS services alongside CMDB platforms, endpoint management tools, identity providers, and third-party scanners.

•	DigiCert® Private CA:
Private certificate authority solution enabling organizations to create, manage, and operate privately trusted root and intermediate CAs for issuing certificates to internal users, devices, servers, and workloads.

•	DigiCert® Software Trust Manager:
A code signing and secure releases solution that provides centralized, policy-driven management of code signing keys and certificates, HSM-backed private key protection, CI/CD pipeline integrations, approval workflows, and comprehensive audit logging. DigiCert ONE environments supporting Software Trust Manager are covered by applicable independent security and compliance attestations, including SOC 2 Type II and WebTrust, depending on the deployment and region. DigiCert uses FIPS 140-2 and/or FIPS 140-3 compliant Hardware Security Modules (HSMs), as applicable, to protect cryptographic keys. Software Trust Manager helps organizations secure software signing and release processes, enforce signing policies, protect signing keys, and strengthen software release security.

frc-cso-pkg.agency_use_case_detail:
VirtualDojo AI CRM targets two federal markets and is intended for direct
use by federal agencies (MKT-IIP-AGU Direct Use).

Federal agencies: the platform is designed for direct agency adoption to
manage customer-relationship, procurement, and contract workflows and the
Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) involved integrated into a federal
information system under 44 U.S.C. 3506 and receiving an agency Authorization
to Operate once FedRAMP Certification is achieved.

Federal contractors: contractors performing on federal contract vehicles
(e.g., GSA Schedules, NASA SEWP VI, Army ITES) must, under DFARS 252.204-7012
and CMMC, host the CUI generated in contract performance in a cloud service
meeting the FedRAMP Moderate baseline. VirtualDojo AI CRM is built to satisfy
that requirement, maintaining federal CUI generated on behalf of those
agencies through their contractors.

Status: VirtualDojo is pursuing FedRAMP 20x Certification (Class C, Program
path) at the Moderate impact level and is in the Initial Implementation
Phase. It has not completed a FedRAMP assessment and holds no agency ATO yet;
this listing will be updated as agency adoption is confirmed.

faq.a: All customer data is stored and processed within the United States in Google Cloud under Assured Workloads (DATA_BOUNDARY_FOR_FEDRAMP_MODERATE). The primary region is us-central1 and disaster-recovery backups are replicated to us-east4; both are inside the same FedRAMP Moderate Assured Workloads enclave, so data never leaves the US boundary. All copies are encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMEK).
Data is encrypted at rest with customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) in Google Cloud KMS, and in transit with TLS 1.2+. Cryptography uses FIPS 140-validated modules.

faq.q: What compliance frameworks do you follow?
faq.a: VirtualDojo is pursuing FedRAMP 20x Certification (Class C) and a SOC 2 (Security) examination. The service is built on Google Cloud and Microsoft services that hold FedRAMP authorizations. Current status is shown on this page.

faq.q: Is VirtualDojo FedRAMP High or Moderate?
faq.a: VirtualDojo AI CRM is assessed to the FedRAMP Moderate baseline via FedRAMP 20x Certification Class C, which matches the Controlled Unclassified Information the service handles. It runs inside Google Cloud's Assured Workloads FedRAMP Moderate boundary and inherits Google's Moderate infrastructure authorization. The application's own certification is in progress.
Google Cloud, Microsoft, SendGrid, Stripe, and GitHub. Each subprocessor, its purpose, the data it handles, and its location are listed in the Subprocessors section above.

Access requires multi-factor authentication and Conditional Access via Microsoft Entra ID, enforces role-based access control and least privilege, and is continuously monitored by the automated KSI validator.

faq.q: How do you handle security incidents?
faq.a: VirtualDojo maintains documented incident-response procedures with continuous monitoring and defined notification timelines. Suspected incidents can be reported to security@virtualdojo.com.

Service availability is measured by a Google Cloud uptime check on app.virtualdojo.com, and 46 Key Security Indicators are validated nightly in-boundary. A rolling availability percentage publishes on this page as monitoring history accrues.

faq.q: What data does the service handle?
faq.a: The service handles Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) including government contract data, customer PII, proposal documents, and pricing data, at the FedRAMP Moderate impact level.

faq.q: How can a federal agency access the full certification package?
faq.a: The Certification Package (Certification Package Overview, Security Decision Record, and Ongoing Certification Reports) is available through authenticated self-service access at trust.virtualdojo.com/request-access federal (.gov/.mil) requesters are granted access automatically; other requests are reviewed under NDA. After signing in, human-readable report pages and the machine-readable JSON are both available under /reports.

whereWeStand: Enablement is listed in the FedRAMP Marketplace under FedRAMP ID FR2628647239 at the Initial Implementation stage. It is not FedRAMP certified and holds zero FedRAMP authorizations. Nothing in this statement claims otherwise.

These counts are recomputed from the rule-by-rule verdict data every time this page is generated, so they can move between quarterly statements; the dated figures elsewhere in this statement stay as written.

All 46 Key Security Indicators report at least one active automated validation method, and 42 of 46 report two or more. Verified against the daily evidence snapshot of 2026-08-11. crossFormatConsistency.howOmissionIsPrevented: Single-sourcing stops the page contradicting the JSON; it does not stop the page omitting part of it, which is the failure that actually occurred when availability endpoints were added to the document after the HTML tables were written. An automated comparison walks every value in each JSON document and confirms it reached the page, so a new field must be either rendered or added to a named exemption list carrying its reason.
crossFormatConsistency.howStalenessIsPrevented: Structurally, not procedurally. Each human-readable page is RENDERED FROM the machine-readable document at request time and is handed no other source of facts — no database handle, no second query, no cached copy. A stale HTML rendering is therefore not a state this service can be in.
crossFormatConsistency.howToVerifyIndependently: Fetch both formats and compare them yourself. The provider's release checks fail on any divergence, and its automated tests re-run the comparison across an outage, a measurement gap, a partial day, a single-endpoint window and an empty log.
crossFormatConsistency.limitationsOfThisCheck: For the trust and status pages it runs at release time, not on every request, so it gates a release rather than a response. For Significant Change Notifications and the Security Decision Record it also runs on every request, and a page that would leave out a value is withheld: notifications are written by hand and can be published without a release, and the Security Decision Record carries live evidence that changes between releases. It compares values one way (every JSON scalar must appear in the HTML); the reverse needs no check because the page has no other source. Booleans and nulls are matched by field rather than by literal, since a page renders them as words.

serviceIdentification.description:
**Enablement®: Own your compliance. Send nothing out. Need no experts, no AI.**

Most compliance platforms make you hire specialists, wire in third-party services, and increasingly hand your data to AI you cannot audit. Enablement flips that. It is a self-contained, deterministic, zero-trust platform where your teams build and run everything visually, and nothing ever leaves your boundary.

1. **No-code process building. No developers, no AI, no token bills.** Business users design complete workflows (BPMN) visually and get web and mobile interfaces generated automatically. No coding, no integration team, no consultants. The engine is deterministic rather than generative: it never hallucinates, never invents an answer, and costs nothing per token. What you design is exactly what runs, the same way every time, fully auditable.
2. **Deploy anywhere. True portability.** Run Enablement in any commercial cloud, any government cloud, your own data center, or as a fully self-contained appliance. No cloud lock-in, no vendor-specific dependency. Move it, mirror it, or air-gap it.
3. **Rapid CMMC Level 2 compliance, with continuous monitoring built in.** CMMC Level 2 readiness comes out of the box, backed by native, always-on continuous monitoring. No separate scanning products to buy, license, or integrate. Assess, monitor, and produce authorization evidence from day one, on a single system.
4. **A genuine zero-trust boundary. Your data never touches a third party.** Your source code lives in its own repository. No data is sent to any outside service for authentication, code analysis, container scanning, file scanning, or continuous monitoring. Nothing is shipped to a SaaS, a scanning vendor, or an AI provider. What happens in your boundary stays in your boundary.
5. **Access control and document marking that remove human error.** Fine-grained role-based and attribute-based access control (RBAC and ABAC) governs exactly who can see and do what. Documents are marked automatically to federal standards (DoW and NARA). No manual labeling, no inconsistent tags, no mislabeled files. The platform does the marking so people cannot get it wrong.
6. **Stop data leaks before they happen.** Human error is the number one cause of data spillage. Enablement checks every share and warns before a document reaches unauthorized personnel, catching the mistake at the moment of sharing rather than after a breach. A potential disclosure, and the liability that follows, becomes a blocked action.
7. **Every authentication method, and your password never reaches the server.** Passkeys, single sign-on (SSO), authenticator apps, email, and more. The password is proven with a challenge-response, so the secret never leaves the user's device; the server stores only a verifier and salt, never the password or any recoverable form of it. Strong, flexible, phishing-resistant sign-in without ever transmitting the credential.
8. **One control set, three frameworks.** Policies and controls are written once and mapped to FedRAMP 20x Key Security Indicators, CMMC Level 2 practices, and SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria. A Section 508 Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT 2.5) is available on request. Built by CMMI-appraised, ISO-certified Advent.

**Intended agency use.** Enablement is intended for both FedRAMP use cases: direct use by agency customers, and indirect use as a third-party information resource inside other cloud service offerings that agencies use directly.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
**Enablement®: Own your compliance. Send nothing out. Need no experts, no AI.**

Most compliance platforms make you hire specialists, wire in third-party services, and increasingly hand your data to AI you cannot audit. Enablement flips that. It is a self-contained, deterministic, zero-trust platform where your teams build and run everything visually, and nothing ever leaves your boundary.

1. **No-code process building. No developers, no AI, no token bills.** Business users design complete workflows (BPMN) visually and get web and mobile interfaces generated automatically. No coding, no integration team, no consultants. The engine is deterministic rather than generative: it never hallucinates, never invents an answer, and costs nothing per token. What you design is exactly what runs, the same way every time, fully auditable.
2. **Deploy anywhere. True portability.** Run Enablement in any commercial cloud, any government cloud, your own data center, or as a fully self-contained appliance. No cloud lock-in, no vendor-specific dependency. Move it, mirror it, or air-gap it.
3. **Rapid CMMC Level 2 compliance, with continuous monitoring built in.** CMMC Level 2 readiness comes out of the box, backed by native, always-on continuous monitoring. No separate scanning products to buy, license, or integrate. Assess, monitor, and produce authorization evidence from day one, on a single system.
4. **A genuine zero-trust boundary. Your data never touches a third party.** Your source code lives in its own repository. No data is sent to any outside service for authentication, code analysis, container scanning, file scanning, or continuous monitoring. Nothing is shipped to a SaaS, a scanning vendor, or an AI provider. What happens in your boundary stays in your boundary.
5. **Access control and document marking that remove human error.** Fine-grained role-based and attribute-based access control (RBAC and ABAC) governs exactly who can see and do what. Documents are marked automatically to federal standards (DoW and NARA). No manual labeling, no inconsistent tags, no mislabeled files. The platform does the marking so people cannot get it wrong.
6. **Stop data leaks before they happen.** Human error is the number one cause of data spillage. Enablement checks every share and warns before a document reaches unauthorized personnel, catching the mistake at the moment of sharing rather than after a breach. A potential disclosure, and the liability that follows, becomes a blocked action.
7. **Every authentication method, and your password never reaches the server.** Passkeys, single sign-on (SSO), authenticator apps, email, and more. The password is proven with a challenge-response, so the secret never leaves the user's device; the server stores only a verifier and salt, never the password or any recoverable form of it. Strong, flexible, phishing-resistant sign-in without ever transmitting the credential.
8. **One control set, three frameworks.** Policies and controls are written once and mapped to FedRAMP 20x Key Security Indicators, CMMC Level 2 practices, and SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria. A Section 508 Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT 2.5) is available on request. Built by CMMI-appraised, ISO-certified Advent.

**Intended agency use.** Enablement is intended for both FedRAMP use cases: direct use by agency customers, and indirect use as a third-party information resource inside other cloud service offerings that agencies use directly.

Live evidence: [FedRAMP Trust Center](https://enablement.cc/ml/20x/trust) · [Secure Configuration Guide](https://enablement.cc/ml/20x/scg) · [enablement.company](https://enablement.company)

servicesNotIncluded.item: Enablement® deployed outside Advent's GovCloud environment
servicesNotIncluded.reason: This certification covers exactly one deployment: the Advent-operated multi-tenant instance in AWS GovCloud us-gov-east-1. The public description correctly says the software is portable to any cloud, to a customer data center, or to a self-contained appliance — none of those customer-operated deployments is inside this authorization boundary or covered by this certification.

Physically separate host holding synthetic data only; no federal customer data. Note the CI/CD pipeline that deploys to production runs on that host and IS in scope — the test application environment is not.

Customer premise equipment, customer browsers and devices, the customer's own SSO identity provider, and customer logging systems are outside the provider boundary. The interfaces to them are in scope; the systems themselves are not.
Developer workstations and source-code analysis tooling process no federal customer data and sit outside the boundary; the development team has no access to production inside the boundary.

certified.compensatingControls: US-persons environment. Root account MFA enabled and no IAM user carries console access, so the control plane is reachable only by key-based programmatic call, verified 2026-08-07.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Inherited controls documented in the SSP; platform firewall manager governs subnet ACLs; encryption at rest through KMS and in transit through TLS. All four EBS volumes verified encrypted on 2026-08-07.
certified.name: AWS GovCloud (US)
certified.useCase: Hosts the entire offering. EC2, S3, KMS, IAM, Config, GuardDuty, CloudTrail, CloudWatch and networking in us-gov-east-1. AWS Inspector and AWS Security Hub are not used.

certified.compensatingControls: No federal customer data and no file content leaves the boundary by this path. A one-time passcode is single-use and time-boxed, and is not sufficient to authenticate on its own.
certified.mitigationMeasures: SMTP STARTTLS enforced. Message bodies are categorical only: an alert says that something happened, never what, and any detail requires the recipient to authenticate to the platform.
certified.name: Amazon SES (commercial, us-east-1)
certified.useCase: Outbound notification and one-time-passcode delivery. GovCloud cannot call the commercial SES API from inside the boundary, so delivery egresses to the AWS US East/West authorized environment.

nonCertified.compensatingControls: A failover DNS flip is a documented manual recovery step rather than an automatic one, so a zone change is a deliberate operator action. Certificates are issued and renewed by Let's Encrypt through certbot on the host, so a DNS compromise alone does not yield a trusted certificate.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: DNSSEC signing is enabled on the enablement.cc hosted zone (ServeSignature SIGNING, verified 2026-08-07), which supersedes the 'not enabled' entry at §9.2 svc-route53-dnssec. Zone changes are restricted to key-based programmatic access; the account has no console-enabled IAM user and root MFA is enabled.
nonCertified.name: Amazon Route 53 (commercial account)
nonCertified.useCase: Authoritative DNS for enablement.cc. Route 53 is not available in GovCloud, so the zone is hosted in the commercial account. DNS carries no customer data.

nonCertified.compensatingControls: Feeds carry detection content, never customer data. A poisoned feed degrades detection rather than granting access, and feed staleness is itself monitored.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures: Pull-only over HTTPS 443. Nothing is pushed outward and no feed provider is granted inbound access. Content is digitally signed and validated before install.
nonCertified.name: Vendor definition and threat-intelligence feeds
nonCertified.provider: Greenbone Community Feed, ClamAV signature mirrors, Trivy vulnerability database, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
nonCertified.useCase: Scanner, anti-virus and vulnerability-prioritization content updates. Required for detection efficacy; without them the continuous-monitoring capability degrades silently.

thirdPartyInformationResources.schemaNote: certified[] carries the schema-required fedRampCertifiedThirdPartyInformationResource (the FedRAMP ID) and useCase. mitigationMeasures, compensatingControls, name, provider, fedRampClass, marketplaceUrl and reference are additional properties. MAS-CSO-TPR requires the mitigation and compensating-control attributes, and the pinned FedRAMP CPO schema (fedramp-certification-package-overview-schema-2026-06-24.json) defines no field for either; when it does, these move into it. This is the same pattern used for securityCategory under certifiedServicesNote.
thirdPartyInformationResources.sourceOfRecord: MINIMUM_ASSESSMENT_SCOPE.md §5, reconciled against §9.2. Edit that table, not this structure.

trustCenterAccessLogging.logged: Every access to every /20x/* endpoint, public and token-gated alike, is recorded with endpoint, outcome, client IP, and timestamp.
trustCenterAccessLogging.retentionEnforcement: Stated policy, not yet machine-enforced at write time. No purge job, TTL, scheduled event, or partition-drop targets the trust-center access log, so records currently accumulate indefinitely — retention is achieved by the absence of deletion rather than by an enforced retention job. The log began on 2026-07-11, so a full 6-month retention period has not yet elapsed and cannot yet be demonstrated by observation. What IS enforced is DETECTION: every /20x/access-log-summary response recomputes a retentionIntegrity verdict that compares the oldest surviving record against the code-pinned table-creation watermark and against the six-month floor, and reports BREACH if a record that must still exist has gone. See retentionIntegrity and the retentionDemonstrated flag in /20x/access-log-summary for the live answer rather than trusting this sentence.
trustCenterAccessLogging.retentionPolicy: Advent retains trust-center access summaries for at least 24 months from the date of access, which exceeds the 6-month CDS-TRC-ACL floor. Records are never purged earlier for convenience, capacity, or at a consumer's request.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
**Service Description**

The GSSOne Azure is a General Support System (GSS) operated by Project Hosts and deployed within Azure Government. The platform is designed as a secure, multi-tenant PaaS/SaaS environment that enables federal, DoD, state, local, and tribal agencies, as well as government contractors, members of the DIB and the public to deploy and operate applications in compliance with federal security requirements.

The GSSOne Azure Core provides a standardized set of centrally managed services that support secure application deployment and operations, including access control, authentication, auditing, monitoring, scanning, patching, configuration management, malware prevention, intrusion prevention, incident response, backup, and disaster recovery.

These capabilities are implemented and managed by Project Hosts and are leveraged by applications deployed on the platform to meet security and compliance requirements.

The GSSOne Azure supports two primary application deployment models:

**1. Applications Included Within the GSS One Authorization Boundary**

Certain SaaS applications are incorporated directly into the GSSOne Azure authorization boundary and are assessed and certified as part of the GSSOne Azure system.

The following SaaS applications are currently included within the GSSOne Azure authorization boundary:

1. **GSSOne User Portal/Admin Page**
1. **GSSOne Command Center (GSSOCC)**
1. **GSS One Azure Support Center**
1. **Quest Security Management Platform (Quest-SMP)**
1. **OnePlan**

More information on each of these along with other certified GSSOne Core/ consumable services can be found in the certified services section below.

**2. Applications Supported on the Platform**

GSSOne Azure also supports customer and Independent Software Vendor (ISV) applications that are deployed on the platform but maintain their own authorization boundary (e.g., agency ATO or ISV-owned system).

In this model, Project Hosts provides the underlying infrastructure, security services, and operational support, while the application owner maintains responsibility for their system authorization and application-specific controls.

This flexible deployment model allows agencies to either leverage existing SaaS capabilities or deploy their own applications within a secure, FedRAMP-authorized environment.

Each of the systems below have been vetted and meets the FedRAMP requirements and are ready to pursue FedRAMP certification or have been certified under their own listing and are viewable under the dependent product list.

Examples of supported applications include:

    - Archive360 (Archive360 Platform)
    - AudioCodes (AudioCodes Live Platform)
    - AvePoint (AvePoint Online Services for US Government)
    - Aztec (Aztec Learning System)
    - Bingli (Bingli)
    - Blue Prism (Blue Prism)

    - Feith Systems and Software Inc. (RMA iQ™)
    - FlowVU (FlowVU Collaboration)
    - Idea Entity (RhyBus Platform)
    - Image Trend (Elite, Report Writer (RW), Continuum (CT), Licensure, Slate)
    - Invoke (UiPath Orchestrator and RPA)
    - Ivanti (MDM, Access, Neurons)

    - ProSymmetry
    - Relocation Management Worldwide (Virtual Employee Network)
    - Synergist Technology, LLC (AFFIRM Solution for AI Compliance, SAS® VIYA®)
    - Teamviewer (TeamViewer Digital Employee Experience (TMV DEX) for Government)
    - UMT360 (SharePoint-based Enterprise Portfolio Management)

    - Wellspring (Accolade Enterprise Innovation Management, Sophia, Evolve)
    - WordPress (WordPress CMS)
    - WordPress As a Service (WPaaS)

For each of these applications, Project Hosts provides deployment, security, and operational support services for these applications, enabling customers to leverage the GSSOne Azure platform while maintaining flexibility in how their systems are authorized and managed. Performing these functions on the partner’s behalf allows the software vendors to focus on their core business model in delivering a secure, highly functional application to the agency while Project Hosts handles the security/ compliance requirements.

**Additional Services**

For customers not deployed on the GSS One Azure, Project Hosts offers dedicated continuous monitoring services leveraging the GSS One Azure Command Center and scanners operated by Project Hosts engineers to configure, scan and provide continuous monitoring services to those external customers and their respective agencies to meet FedRAMP requirements.

**Certified Services**

The following services are included as Certified Services within the GSSOne Azure certification. Unless otherwise noted, each service operates within the GSSOne Azure authorization boundary at the **High** security impact level and under **Certification Class D**.

**GSSOne Azure Core**

    - **Date Available:** March 11, 2016
    - **Security Impact Level:** High
    - **Certification Class:** D

The GSSOne Azure Core provides a standardized set of centrally managed services that support secure application deployment and operations, including access control, authentication, auditing, monitoring, scanning, patching, configuration management, malware prevention, intrusion prevention, incident response, backup, and disaster recovery.

**GSSOne Command Center**

    - **Date Available:** May 5, 2025
    - **Security Impact Level:** High
    - **Certification Class:** D

The GSS One Command Center is a centralized compliance and operations platform that gives agencies and CSP partners real-time visibility into system security, risk, and authorization status. Designed to meet FedRAMP Rev. 5 BIRs and aligned with the direction of FedRAMP 20x, the GSSOCC supports a shift toward continuous, evidence-driven validation rather than static, point-in-time assessments.

It serves as a single pane of glass for managing the full lifecycle of authorization and operations, bringing together system documentation, vulnerability data, incident tracking, change control, and monitoring into one integrated experience. By linking controls directly to supporting evidence and operational data, the GSSOCC reduces the overhead of maintaining compliance and enables faster, more transparent ATO decisions for agencies.

**GSSOne Support Center**

    - **Date Available:** May 5, 2025
    - **Security Impact Level:** High
    - **Certification Class:** D

Project Hosts has configured a customer-facing support portal for creating and managing support tickets powered by Atlassian Jira. This allows customers to view all of their relevant tickets, create tickets, submit change control requests, upload screenshots, review knowledgebases and communicate with PH staff through a secure channel.

    - **Date Available:** March 11, 2016
    - **Security Impact Level:** High
    - **Certification Class:** D

    - **Date Available:** March 11, 2016
    - **Security Impact Level:** High
    - **Certification Class:** D

Provides centrally managed email relay and routing services for applications operating within the authorization boundary. The service supports controlled delivery, encryption, authentication, logging, and monitoring of system-generated email.

    - **Date Available:** March 11, 2016
    - **Security Impact Level:** High
    - **Certification Class:** D

Provides centralized certificate issuance, validation, renewal, revocation, and lifecycle management for system components. It supports trusted encrypted communications and consistent certificate governance across the environment.

    - **Date Available:** March 11, 2016
    - **Security Impact Level:** High
    - **Certification Class:** D

Automates the generation, deployment, renewal, and tracking of TLS certificates used by authorized applications and infrastructure. Automation reduces expired-certificate risk while supporting approved cryptographic and certificate-management requirements.

**GSSOne Illumination/Inventory**

    - **Date Available:** May 5, 2025
    - **Security Impact Level:** High
    - **Certification Class:** D

Provides automated discovery and inventory of cloud resources, configurations, and security-relevant attributes within the environment. The service supports continuous compliance validation, evidence generation, configuration-drift identification, and centralized reporting.

**Quest Security Management Platform**

    - **Date Available:** June 24, 2026
    - **Security Impact Level:** High
    - **Certification Class:** D

The Quest-SMP is a browser-based application with different agents that can be deployed on the agency devices/systems based on their individual use case.

The Quest-SMP contains two major components:

    - **Quest Identity Recovery for Entra ID: **Quest Identity Recovery for Entra ID is a SaaS-based backup and recovery solution for Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 that extends protection beyond native Microsoft tools. It enables fast, secure restoration of users, groups, attributes, and memberships from a single cloud interface. Administrators can compare backups, view changes, and recover only what’s needed—reducing manual errors and downtime. All recovery actions are logged and auditable to support compliance requirements. Hybrid Active Directory and Entra ID recovery is also supported through built-in integration with on-premises Quest Recovery Manager for Active Directory. Delivered as a secure, high-availability cloud service, Quest Identity Recovery for Entra ID helps federal agencies simplify directory recovery, maintain continuity, and meet governance standards without the need for on-premises infrastructure.
    - **Quest Identity Defense**: Quest Identity Defense is a hybrid Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID security and audit platform that helps federal agencies strengthen identity threat detection, containment, and response while reducing risk of exposure and downtime. It identifies Tier Zero and other privileged objects across Active Directory and Entra ID to pinpoint where the greatest risks reside. The platform continually assesses identity environments for problematic configurations and drift from best-practice baselines, helping maintain compliance and operational integrity. Quest Identity Defense provides enhanced threat detection and observability for directory changes and protects Tier Zero assets from malicious in-memory modification—supporting zero trust and mission continuity across hybrid identity systems.

**OnePlan**

    - **Date Available:** September 21, 2026
    - **Security Impact Level:** High
    - **Certification Class:** D

OnePlan is a strategic portfolio and work management platform that helps federal agencies plan, prioritize, and execute mission-critical initiatives. It enables Program Management Offices (PMOs) to align projects, resources, and budgets to mission priorities, with centralized, audit-ready visibility across projects, programs, and portfolios.

Built for Microsoft, OnePlan integrates with various Microsoft SaaS products enabling agencies to work within their existing Microsoft ecosystem while maintaining centralized governance across portfolio and work data. By consolidating portfolio, project, and resource management in a single platform, OnePlan gives agency leaders the visibility and control needed to align investments to mission outcomes.

GSSOne Azure also serves as an underlying authorized platform for applications and cloud service offerings that leverage GSSOne Azure security, infrastructure, and operational capabilities. Depending on the application deployment and authorization model, these relationships may be represented as included Certified Services, dependent products, reuse relationships, or separately authorized customer systems.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
CMMC Space is a multi-tenant SaaS virtual desktop service hosted in Google Cloud’s FedRAMP High environment for defense contractors and other organizations that handle Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). It gives those customers a VDI environment for processing CUI and for access to FedRAMP-authorized services, so they can handle that CUI in line with NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC Level 2.

Users sign in using the Google Identity Platform into a session ATX Defense builds and hardens: a locked-down Chrome browser or a mission-specific virtual environment, streamed over HTML5. Each customer is a separate tenant with its own users, groups, and workspace images. The underlying virtual infrastructure is operated and patched by ATX Defense, so contractors do not stand up and maintain the environment themselves.

The CUI in scope is what customers process, store, or transmit inside the virtual desktops and the collaboration services reached from them. The user's own device runs only a browser and stays outside that boundary.

certified.name: AWS GovCloud (US)
certified.useCase: AWS GovCloud (US) hosts VisualVault Cloud's infrastructure for the government-exclusive offering.
certified.justification: Provides FedRAMP-authorized infrastructure in U.S. government-only regions operated by screened U.S. persons, meeting federal customer requirements for data location and handling.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Controls are inherited from the AWS GovCloud (US) FedRAMP authorization (package F1603047866). Customer data is encrypted at rest with VisualVault-managed AWS KMS keys and in transit with TLS 1.2 or higher; resources are segmented into VPCs with security groups permitting only required traffic.
certified.compensatingControls: Least-privilege IAM roles with multi-factor authentication for administrators; AWS CloudTrail and GuardDuty monitoring forwarded to the SIEM; AWS Config recording with a daily automated asset inventory; and encrypted backups replicated across GovCloud regions.

certified.name: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure Government)
certified.useCase: Microsoft Entra ID (via Azure Government) provides internal corporate single sign-on for personnel accessing VisualVault Cloud.
certified.justification: Centralizes identity for VisualVault personnel so administrative access to VisualVault Cloud is granted, reviewed and revoked in one place with enforced multi-factor authentication.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Controls are inherited from the Microsoft Azure Government FedRAMP authorization (package F1603087869). Entra ID authenticates VisualVault personnel only; it does not store or process federal customer data.
certified.compensatingControls: Multi-factor authentication required for all administrative sign-ins; conditional access limits administrative sign-in; access is reviewed periodically and removed promptly at offboarding; sign-in logs are retained for investigation.

certified.name: CrowdStrike Falcon Platform for Government
certified.useCase: CrowdStrike Falcon Platform for Government provides endpoint detection and response across VisualVault's corporate AWS and AWS GovCloud infrastructure, via separate subscriptions for each environment.
certified.justification: Provides continuous endpoint detection and response across VisualVault Cloud hosts, supporting rapid detection and containment of malicious activity.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Controls are inherited from the CrowdStrike Falcon Platform for Government FedRAMP authorization (package FR1807853629A). Sensors send security telemetry (process, file and network metadata), not federal customer content, over TLS; the government-environment subscription is kept separate from the corporate one.
certified.compensatingControls: Access to the Falcon console is restricted to the security team with multi-factor authentication; detections are triaged under the Incident Response Process; sensor coverage is verified against the automated asset inventory.

certified.name: KnowBe4 Platform
certified.useCase: KnowBe4 Platform provides security awareness training for VisualVault personnel.
certified.justification: Delivers and records required security awareness and role-based training for VisualVault personnel with access to the system.
certified.mitigationMeasures: Controls are inherited from the KnowBe4 FedRAMP authorization (package FR2201340492). The platform holds personnel training records only, never federal customer data, and has no connection to VisualVault Cloud systems.
certified.compensatingControls: Administrative access to KnowBe4 is limited to training administrators; completion is validated automatically by the training validators reported in the Security Decision Record; records are retained per policy.

source.evidenceName: Generating Inventories - AWS GovCloud Asset Inventory

informationResourceInventory.derivation: This list is generated automatically, not maintained by hand. aws_govcloud_asset_inventory.py 2.0.0 runs on a schedule with read-only AWS API calls across us-gov-east-1, us-gov-west-1 (and global services such as IAM, S3 and Route 53) and records every resource found in a machine-readable inventory, stored with its SHA-256 integrity hash as evidence "Generating Inventories - AWS GovCloud Asset Inventory" (EVD-AWS-GOVCLOUD-INVENTORY) in VisualVault's FedRAMP evidence repository. Each refresh of this Certification Package Overview reads the newest inventory and summarizes it by AWS service and resource type. No inventoried resource carries a FedRAMPBoundary tag, so every resource in the inventoried AWS account is treated as part of the cloud service offering (979 resources). Resource names, network addresses and identifiers are deliberately not reproduced here; the complete inventory and the code that produces it are available to assessors.

independentAssessment.overallSummaryOfAssessment:
## Scope
A-LIGN performed an independent FedRAMP 20x Class B assessment of VisualVault Cloud against the FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026. The assessment covered all Key Security Indicators and FedRAMP rules applicable to a 20x Class B certification, including the cloud service offering, the third-party information resources it relies on, and the personnel and processes that operate it.

## Approach
A-LIGN verified and validated each KSI and rule through examination of provider-supplied evidence and, where applicable, testing of technical telemetry and configuration data. Evidence was delivered through the provider's continuous evidence pipeline in Paramify, allowing A-LIGN to assess the current operating state of the cloud service offering rather than point-in-time documentation alone. Each KSI and rule was evaluated against the current rule text and its Class B applicability. All evidence was reviewed by the lead assessor and an independent second reviewer. Results for each KSI and rule are recorded in the Security Decision Record.

## Results
Based on the procedures performed, A-LIGN determined that VisualVault Cloud satisfies the KSIs and FedRAMP rules applicable to a 20x Class B certification. Issues identified during the assessment were remediated by the provider and re-validated by A-LIGN prior to completion. No failures remain open.

## Areas of Dispute
There are no areas of dispute between A-LIGN and VisualVault.

relevantPolicies.name: Physical and Environmental Protection Policy (POLICY-0010)
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for physical and environmental protection of information systems, based on NIST SP 800-53 (Moderate) controls. It covers infrastructure hosting requirements (FedRAMP-authorized IaaS), alternate work site/remote access rules such as VPN and encryption requirements, and controls over the delivery and removal of equipment from VisualVault facilities.

relevantPolicies.name: Security Assessment and Authorization Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy defines requirements for security assessment and authorization of information systems, based on NIST SP 800-53 (Moderate) controls. It covers independent and internal security assessments, system interconnections, plans of actions and milestones, security authorization, and continuous monitoring, including coordination with FedRAMP JAB/AO and third-party assessors.

relevantPolicies.name: SOP-0030 - Information Release
relevantPolicies.summary: This procedure establishes controls to prevent unintended disclosure or spillage of information when VisualVault posts content to publicly accessible systems. It defines authorized personnel and locations for public postings, a review/approval workflow, and additional safeguards (redaction, NDAs, encryption) for releasing sensitive or confidential information such as during sales cycles.

relevantPolicies.name: VisualVault Audit and Accountability Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy (Policy-0013) establishes VisualVault's requirements for auditing and accountability across its information systems, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) and NIST SP 800-92 guidelines. It defines requirements for audit scope, event logging, time synchronization, log review/monitoring, protection and retention of audit records, and roles responsible for enforcement and oversight.

relevantPolicies.name: Contingency Planning Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes requirements for contingency planning based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, covering disaster recovery/business continuity plan development, distribution, training, and testing. It also details information system backup requirements, data retention schedules, and data restoration testing procedures.

relevantPolicies.name: POLICY-0019 – Personnel Management Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's personnel management program, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, covering all personnel and third parties using VisualVault systems. It defines a four-level corrective action/sanctions framework for security and confidentiality violations, along with notification, enforcement, and review responsibilities.

relevantPolicies.name: Media Protection Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for handling digital and non-digital media, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls. It covers media access authorization, marking, storage, transport, and sanitization, along with roles, responsibilities, exceptions, and enforcement procedures.

relevantPolicies.name: Access, Identification, and Authentication Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes access control, identification, and authentication requirements based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Moderate) baseline controls. It covers topics such as least privilege, user registration, role-based access control, session/account protections, separation of duties, network access control, external systems, device identification, and multi-factor authentication.

relevantPolicies.name: Personnel Security Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for personnel security based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Moderate) controls, covering position risk designation, personnel screening and rescreening, hiring, training, termination, transfers, and third-party personnel requirements. It defines responsibilities for management, the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance, employees, and third parties to ensure physical and system access is properly authorized and monitored throughout the employment lifecycle.

relevantPolicies.name: Vendor Management Policy
relevantPolicies.fileName: (SR-01) Supply Chain and Vendor Risk Management Policy.pdf
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for managing third-party IT vendors and partners to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of its systems and data. It covers vendor inventory and risk classification, contract security requirements (including for cloud service providers and telecommunications vendors), and change management processes for vendor-provided services.

relevantPolicies.name: Information Security Policy (POLICY-0009)
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes the organization's information security program based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, covering security awareness/training (SETA), incident response and handling, information spillage response, and security planning (system security plan and security architecture). It defines roles and responsibilities (e.g., CTO, Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance) and enforcement procedures for all VisualVault personnel, third parties, and information systems.

relevantPolicies.name: Mobile Device Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes security requirements and user responsibilities for mobile device usage, including laptops, portable devices (tablets/smartphones), and BYOD/POCD devices connecting to corporate systems. It also covers 802.11 Wi-Fi security controls and is based on NIST SP 800-124 guidance, fulfilling NIST 800-53 control AC-19.

relevantPolicies.name: Risk Assessment Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes requirements for risk assessment and vulnerability management based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls. It covers security categorization, periodic risk assessments, vulnerability scanning (external, internal, and change-triggered), scanning tool requirements, vulnerability review, remediation timelines by severity, and reporting to leadership and FedRAMP officials. It also defines roles and responsibilities, primarily for VisualVault Management and the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance.

relevantPolicies.name: Operations Management Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes IT operations security requirements based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, covering system maintenance, boundary and transmission protection, cryptographic key management, and system/information integrity practices such as flaw remediation, malicious code protection, and monitoring. It also defines roles and responsibilities for management, the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance, personnel, and third parties, along with enforcement procedures for policy violations.

relevantPolicies.name: Configuration Management Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy defines requirements for configuration management of information systems based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Moderate) controls. It covers baseline configurations, change control, access restrictions, configuration settings, least functionality, system component inventory, configuration management planning, and software usage/installation restrictions. It also outlines roles, responsibilities, enforcement, and revision history.

relevantPolicies.name: Systems and Services Acquisition Policy (POLICY-0012)
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for acquiring, developing, and testing information systems, components, and services, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Moderate) controls. It covers the system development lifecycle, acquisition process criteria, documentation requirements, external information system services (including FedRAMP, CJIS, and HIPAA considerations), and developer configuration management and security testing obligations. Roles and responsibilities for VisualVault management, the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance, personnel, and third parties are also defined.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Dossier for Government is a cloud-based competency and training management solution for federal agencies. It replaces paper competency folders with a single system of record for defining the competencies each role requires, assessing staff against those requirements on recurring cycles, delivering the training that closes the gaps, and producing current competency status on demand at the team, facility, or department level.

The service is built for federal workforces with recurring, externally driven competency obligations — including clinical and nursing education staff, and healthcare technology management personnel responsible for maintaining and repairing medical equipment. Assessment schedules, advance notifications, and overdue flags are tracked by the system rather than depending on manual review of paper files.

**Services included**

- **Dossier Profile** — the core competency management service. Role-based competency definitions and assigned core tasks, assessments with assessor sign-off and proficiency ratings, configurable reassessment cycles, supporting attachments, automated notification of upcoming and overdue assessments, dashboards and reporting, role-based access control, and audit logging.
- **Dossier Learn** — an integrated learning management system. Course and training assignment, delivery, and completion tracking, linked to the competency requirements held in Dossier Profile.
- **Dossier Development Program** — structured career development supporting clinical ladder programs. Defined advancement levels and criteria, evidence submission against those criteria, and review and progression tracking.

**Security category.** Each included service is categorized Low under FIPS 199 for confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

**Information handled.** Dossier for Government holds employee competency, training, and development records: employee name, work email address, job title and role, facility and organizational unit, assigned core tasks, competency ratings, assessment and due dates, assessor identity, training and course completion records, development program submissions, supporting attachments such as checklists and certifications, account role assignment, and audit logs of user activity.

The service is not intended to hold protected health information, patient or beneficiary records, clinical or treatment data, controlled unclassified information, Social Security numbers, or financial or payment data. Permitted use is defined in the terms of service and in the Secure Configuration Guide.

Dossier for Government is delivered as multi-tenant SaaS.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Apply Government Solutions provides FedHire, the FedRAMP Certified Class C cloud-based talent acquisition platform previously branded as Monster Hiring Management Enterprise (MHME) by Monster Government Solutions. FedHire delivers end-to-end support across the federal hiring and human capital lifecycle, from position classification and vacancy announcement to hiring management and new hire onboarding. As a FedRAMP Certified Class C solution, FedHire is FISMA moderate and built to meet FedRAMP Security Requirements. It meets OMB standards and complies with Section 508 requirements. FedHire is built to integrate across the federal hiring and human capital ecosystem, connecting with systems such as USAJOBS, eOPF, NFC, and IBC - as well as other agency and shared-service platforms - to enable seamless, end-to-end data exchange throughout the hiring lifecycle.

All components of **FedHire** are certified at the Class C (Moderate) impact level and available to all federal agencies:

- **FedHire Hiring Management** is the core applicant tracking system component, integrated with USAJOBS. It supports the creation and posting of job opportunity announcements (JOAs), application management, applicant tracking, candidate referral, and communication among HR staff, hiring managers, and job applicants. It connects to all related FedHire components to support an end-to-end hiring workflow.

- **FedHire Position Classification** uses guided builder wizards with intelligent tools for occupational series and grade-level recommendations to develop position descriptions, functional statements, cover sheets, and evaluation statements, and routes documents through review, approval, and storage workflows with version control and status dashboards. It provides a searchable, agency-specific classification library with document comparison and suggestions, and tracks classification data for reporting.

- **FedHire Job Analysis** facilitates the collaboration between hiring managers and HR teams to document job-specific competencies and appropriate assessment strategies, and links job analysis results to Job Opportunity Announcements (JOAs), crediting plans, and the position description.

- **FedHire Hiring Assessments** provides a framework for delivering external, integrated applicant assessments through third-party assessment providers. The framework is utilized to incorporate standardized, agency-specific, situational-judgment, technical skills, and other assessment methodologies into agency hiring workflows, with assessment results returned to the applicant record to support screening, ranking, and review by HR professionals and hiring managers.

- **FedHire Collaborate** creates and assigns subject matter expert (SME) panels to review and score applicants, centralizing vacancy details, scoring parameters, and applicant materials in one location. It collects numerical ratings and narrative feedback from SMEs, averages or consensus-scores candidates, and combines with other assessments into a weighted cumulative score. HR can review, accept, or return SME ratings, and the module documents panel participants, dates, scores, and comments for audit purposes.

- **FedHire Selecting Official** provides hiring managers (selecting officials) with tools to review job postings, select assessment criteria, review certificates of eligible applicants, submit annotated certificates to HR, and share certificates across their agency and with other agencies that are granted access.

- **FedHire Onboarding / FedHire Onboarding+** (certified 9/25/2025) automates entrance-on-duty processing for new hires, populates onboarding forms from application data, coordinates provisioning across agency departments, and integrates with agency HRIS platforms. Onboarding+ includes and integrates with USAJOBSs’ agency-branded new hire portal and OPM's eOPF. It allows customized agency-branded documents and templates.

- **FedHire Analytics** enables review of audit-enabled vacancies and associated documentation for compliance with HR procedures.

- **FedHire Auditor** enables review of audit-enabled vacancies and associated documentation for compliance with HR procedures.

To learn more about the FedHire talent acquisition system (TAS), visit: https://www.applygovernmentsolutions.com/solutions/fedhire/

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: AWS GovCloud (US) is an AWS Region designed to allow US government agencies and customers supporting the US government to move more sensitive workloads into the cloud. In addition to complying with FedRAMP requirements, the AWS GovCloud (US) framework adheres to U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) regulations. Additional information is available at http://aws.amazon.com/govcloud-us/. AWS GovCloud (US-East) and (US-West) Regions are operated by employees who are U.S. citizens on U.S. soil. AWS GovCloud (US) is only accessible to U.S. entities and root account holders who pass a screening process. The AWS GovCloud (US) network consists of AWS’s internal data center facilities, servers, networking equipment, and host software systems that are within AWS’s reasonable control, which are used to provide AWS services in the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. Federal agencies interested in collaborative continuous monitoring with AWS should reach out to: aws-collaborative-conmon@amazon.com.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription: Amazon Application Programming Interface (API) Gateway is a fully managed service that enables creation of RESTful APIs and WebSocket APIs that enable real-time two-way communication applications. API Gateway supports containerized and serverless workloads, as well as web applications.

Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) helps prepare for and complete recovery of applications running on AWS infrastructure. ARC provides multi-Availability Zone recovery through zonal shift and zonal autoshift, which temporarily move traffic for supported resources away from an impaired Availability Zone to healthy Availability Zones in the same AWS Region, and multi-Region recovery through routing control, which fails over DNS traffic between AWS Regions using highly reliable routing controls and customer-defined safety rules, and readiness check, which monitors application resources across Regions for recovery readiness.

Amazon Athena is an interactive query service that enables analyzation of data in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. Athena is serverless, so there is no infrastructure to manage, and customers pay only for the queries that are run.
Amazon Aurora MySQL provides built-in security, continuous backups, serverless compute, read replicas, automated multi-Region replication, and integrations with other AWS services.
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL is an open source relational database that enables set up, operation, and scale of PostgreSQL deployments on the cloud.

Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that makes foundation models (FMs) from Amazon and leading artificial intelligence (AI) startups available through an API, so various FMs can be chosen that best suited for use cases.

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is the platform to build, connect, and optimize AI agents at scale. Customers can build with any open-source framework and any model. AgentCore enables customers to connect agents to their tools and data with authentication and access controls built in. Customers can monitor and improve agents in production with tracing and evaluation. AgentCore handles the infrastructure so customers can focus on agent logic, not backend plumbing, and provides enterprise-grade security and reliability without giving up open-source flexibility.
Amazon Chime SDK is a set of real-time communications components that developers can use to add messaging, audio, video, screen sharing and telephony capabilities to their applications.
Amazon Cloud Directory enables the build of flexible cloud-native directories for organizing hierarchies of data along multiple dimensions.

Amazon CloudWatch is a monitoring and observability service that provides data and actionable insights to monitor applications, respond to system-wide performance changes, optimize resource utilization, and get a unified view of operational health. CloudWatch collects monitoring and operational data in the form of logs, metrics, and events, providing a unified view of AWS resources, applications, and services that run on AWS and on-premises servers.

CloudWatch Logs enables centralization of logs from all systems, applications, and AWS services in use, in a single, highly scalable service. The logs are viewable, regardless of their source, as a single and consistent flow of events ordered by time, are able to be queried and sorted based on other dimensions, grouped by specific fields, custom computations and visualization dashboards enabled.
Amazon Cognito enables the addition of user sign-up, sign-in, and access control to web and mobile apps.

Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing (NLP) service that uses machine learning to find insights and relationships in text. The service identifies the language of the text; extracts key phrases, places, people, brands, or events; understands how positive or negative the text is; analyzes text using tokenization and parts of speech; and automatically organizes a collection of text files by topic.

Amazon Comprehend Medical is a natural language processing service that uses machine learning to extract relevant medical information from unstructured text. Amazon Comprehend Medical uses advanced machine learning models to accurately and quickly identify medical information, such as medical conditions and medications, and determines their relationship to each other.

Amazon Connect Customer utilized AI agents to reason, act, and drive interactions to resolution - with human agents ready to step in when needed. One intelligent system that learns from every conversation, making the next one better.

Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose reliably loads streaming data into data lakes, data stores, and analytics services. It is a fully managed service that automatically scales to match the throughput of data and requires no ongoing administration. It can also batch, compress, transform, and encrypt data streams before loading, minimizing the amount of storage used and increasing security.

Amazon Detective automatically collects log data from AWS resources and uses machine learning, statistical analysis, and graph theory to build a linked set of data that enables the conduction of security investigations.
Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fully managed, enterprise-ready, database service that is purpose-built for JSON data management at scale.
Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed, multiregion, multimaster, durable database with built-in security, backup and restore, and in-memory caching for internet-scale applications.

Amazon Elastic Cloud Compute (EC2) Image Builder simplifies the building, testing, and deployment of Virtual Machine and container images for use on AWS or on-premises by providing a graphical interface, built-in automation, and AWS-provided security settings.

Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) enables creation of storage volumes and attaches them to Amazon EC2 instances, creating a file system on top of these volumes, run a database, or use them like block storage. Amazon EBS volumes are placed in a specific Availability Zone, where they are automatically replicated to protect from the failure of a single component.

Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) offers a compute platform, with over 1000 instances and choice of processor, storage, networking, operating system, and purchase model to help customers match workload needs.
Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) is a fully-managed Docker container registry that enables developers to store, manage, and deploy Docker container images.

Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) is a fully managed container orchestration service. AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that works with both Amazon ECS and Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS).

Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) is a fully managed elastic NFS file system for use with AWS Cloud services and on-premises resources. Amazon EFS is a regional service storing data within and across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) for high availability and durability. Amazon EC2 instances can access file systems across AZs, regions, and VPCs, while on-premises servers can access using AWS Direct Connect or AWS VPN.
Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) is a fully managed service that enables the build, run, and scale of production-ready Kubernetes applications across environments.
Amazon EMR is a cloud big data platform for processing vast amounts of data using open source tools.

Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory data store that provides sub-millisecond latency to power internet-scale real-time applications. Built on open-source Redis and compatible with the Redis APIs, ElastiCache works with Redis clients and uses the open Redis data format to store data.

Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus that enables building of event-driven applications at scale using events generated from applications, integrated Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) applications, and AWS services.
Amazon FSx is a fully-managed service that supports workloads, enabling the launch, run, and scale of high-performance file systems in the cloud.
Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors for malicious activity and unauthorized behavior to protect AWS accounts, workloads, and data stored in Amazon S3.

Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability management service that continually scans AWS workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. Amazon Inspector automatically discovers running Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances and container images residing in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR), at any scale, and immediately starts assessing them for known vulnerabilities.
Amazon Kendra is a fully managed, intelligent search service powered by machine learning (ML).

Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) is a scalable, highly available, and managed Apache Cassandra compatible database service. Data is encrypted by default and Amazon Keyspaces enabling back-up of table data continuously using point-in-time recovery.

Amazon Kinesis Data Streams (KDS) is a scalable and durable real-time data streaming service that can continuously capture gigabytes of data per second from hundreds of thousands of sources such as website clickstreams, database event streams, financial transactions, social media feeds, IT logs, and location-tracking events. The data enables real-time analytics use cases such as real-time dashboards, real-time anomaly detection, and dynamic pricing.

Amazon Kinesis Video Streams securely streams video from connected devices to AWS for analytics, machine learning (ML), playback, and other processing. Kinesis Video Streams automatically provisions and elastically scales all the infrastructure needed to ingest streaming video data from millions of devices. It durably stores, encrypts, and indexes video data in streams, and allows users to access data through easy-to-use APIs. Kinesis Video Streams enables users to utilize playback video for live, on-demand viewing, and quickly build applications that take advantage of computer vision and video analytics through integration with Amazon Rekognition Video, and libraries for ML.

Amazon Lex is a service for building conversational interfaces into any application using voice and text. Amazon Lex provides the advanced deep learning functionalities of automatic speech recognition (ASR) for converting speech to text, and natural language understanding (NLU) to recognize the intent of the text, enabling the build of applications with highly engaging user experiences and lifelike conversational interactions.

Amazon Location Service is a fully managed service that enables customers to add location functionality to applications securely and privately. Customers are able to visualize data on a map, recommend routes, use geocoding to convert plain text addresses into geographic coordinates, use reverse geocoding to convert latitude and longitude coordinates into addresses, and monitor and track assets.

Amazon Managed Grafana is a fully managed and secure data visualization service that customers can use to instantly query, correlate, and visualize operational metrics, logs, and traces from multiple sources. Customers create logically isolated Grafana servers called workspaces to build dashboards and visualizations without having to deploy any hardware. The service manages provisioning, setup, scaling, and maintenance of Grafana servers and provides built-in security features including single sign-on, data access control, and audit reporting. Amazon Managed Grafana integrates with supported AWS data sources and includes a permission provisioning feature for adding these services as data sources.

certifiedServices.serviceName: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
certifiedServices.serviceDescription: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink transforms and analyzes streaming data in real time. Apache Flink is an open source framework and engine for processing data streams.

Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is a fully managed, multi-cloud, cross-project solution for Prometheus, enabling managed monitoring and alerting that provides data and actionable insights for container environments deployed at scale. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is fully compatible with the popular open-source Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Prometheus project. As an AWS managed service, Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus simplifies the provisioning and setup of Prometheus, automates much of the ongoing operations and maintenance, and automatically adjusts as container workloads scale up and down.

certifiedServices.serviceName: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK)
certifiedServices.serviceDescription: Amazon MSK is a fully managed, open-source platform for building real-time streaming data pipelines and applications that enables population of data lakes, streams changes to and from databases, and powers machine learning and analytics applications.

Amazon MemoryDB is a Redis-compatible, durable, in-memory database service is compatible with Redis, enabling the build of applications using the same flexible and friendly Redis data structures, APIs, and commands that they already use today.

Amazon MQ is a managed message broker service for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ that enables easy to set up and operate message brokers on AWS. Amazon MQ reduces operational responsibilities by managing the provisioning, setup, and maintenance of message brokers.

Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database service that enables the build and run of applications that work with highly connected datasets. The core of Neptune is a purpose-built, high-performance graph database engine optimized for storing billions of relationships and querying the graph with milliseconds latency.
Amazon OpenSearch Service is a fully-managed service that delivers APIs and real-time analytics capabilities enabling  availability, scalability, and security for production workloads.

certifiedServices.serviceName: Amazon Pinpoint and End User Messaging
certifiedServices.serviceDescription: Amazon Pinpoint and End User Messaging is a flexible and scalable outbound and inbound marketing communications service.

Amazon Polly is a service that turns text into lifelike speech, the creation of applications that talk, and the build of entirely new categories of speech-enabled products. Polly's Text-to-Speech (TTS) service uses advanced deep learning technologies to synthesize natural sounding human speech.

Amazon Quick Suite is a fully managed, cloud-powered business intelligence service that answers questions and turns those answers into actions using agentic teammates for research, business insights, and automation.

Amazon RDS manages complex database administrative tasks, such as provisioning, patching, backups, recovery, failure detection, and repair. With Amazon RDS for Db2, users can choose bring-your-own-license model to move on-premises Db2 databases to the cloud with existing IBM Db2 licenses.
Amazon RDS for MariaDB is an open source relational database created by the original developers of MySQL. Amazon RDS enables set up, operation, and scale of MariaDB server deployments in the cloud.
Amazon RDS for MySQL is an open source relational database to enable set up, operation, and scale of MySQL deployments in the cloud.
Amazon RDS for Oracle is a fully managed commercial database to enable set up, operation, and scale Oracle deployments in the cloud.
Amazon RDS for Postgres is an open source relational database to enable set up, operation, and scale of Postgres deployments in the cloud.
Amazon RDS for SQL multi-AZ deployments provide enhanced availability and durability for RDS database (DB) instances.
Amazon Redshift is a managed data warehousing and analytics service that automates the administrative tasks associated with provisioning, configuring, and monitoring a data warehouse.

Amazon Rekognition enables the addition of image and video analysis to applications using proven, highly scalable, deep learning technology to identify objects, people, text, scenes, and activities in images and videos, as well as detect any inappropriate content.

Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service designed to provide a way to route end users to Internet applications by translating names like www.example.com into the numeric IP addresses like 192.0.2.1 that computers use to connect to each other.

Amazon S3 Glacier and S3 Glacier Deep Archive are secure, durable Amazon S3 cloud storage classes for data archiving and long-term backup. They are designed to deliver 99.999999999% durability, and provide comprehensive security and compliance capabilities that can help meet the most stringent regulatory requirements.

Amazon SageMaker AI is a fully managed service that provides developers and data scientists with the ability to build, train, and deploy machine learning (ML) models quickly. SageMaker AI supports governance requirements with simplified access control and transparency over ML projects. In addition, users can build foundation models (FMs), large models that were trained on massive datasets, with purpose-built tools to fine-tune, experiment, retrain, and deploy FMs.

Amazon Security Lake is a service that automates the sourcing, aggregation, normalization, and data management of security data across the organization into a security data lake stored in the customers account. A security data lake helps make the organizations security data broadly accessible to their preferred security analytics solutions to power use cases such as threat detection, investigation, and incident response.
Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) is a flexible and scalable email service that enables developers to send mail from within any application.

Amazon Simple Notification Service (SNS) is a fully managed messaging service for both system-to-system and app-to-person (A2P) communication enabling communication between systems through publish/subscribe (pub/sub) patterns that enable messaging between decoupled microservice applications or to communicate directly to users via SMS, mobile push and email.
Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service that enables decoupling and scale of microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications.

Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) is storage for the internet, that is highly scalable, durable, and available distributed object store designed for mission-critical and primary data storage. S3 stores objects redundantly on multiple devices across multiple facilities and is designed to protect data and allow access, even in the case of a failure of a data center.
Amazon SWF helps developers build, run, and scale background jobs that have parallel or sequential steps.

Amazon Textract is a fully managed machine learning service that automatically extracts text and data from scanned documents that goes beyond simple optical character recognition (OCR) to identify, understand, and extract data from forms and tables.

Amazon Timestream for LiveAnalytics enables lifecycle management of time-series data by keeping recent data in memory and moving historical data to a cost-optimized storage tier based on user-defined policies.

Amazon Transcribe uses a deep learning process called automatic speech recognition (ASR) to convert speech to text quickly and accurately. Amazon Transcribe can be used to transcribe customer service calls, to automate closed captioning and subtitling, and to generate metadata for media assets to create a fully searchable archive.

Amazon Translate is a neural machine translation service that delivers language translation. Neural machine translation is a form of language translation automation that uses deep learning models to deliver more accurate and more natural sounding translation than traditional statistical and rule-based translation algorithms.

Amazon Verified Permissions is a fully managed authorization service that uses the provably correct Cedar policy language, enabling users to build secure applications. With Verified Permissions, users can build applications by externalizing authorization and centralizing policy management as well as aligning authorization within the application with Zero Trust principles. Amazon Verified Permissions also enables Security and audit teams to analyze and audit who has access to what within applications.
Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) enables the provisioning of a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud to launch AWS resources in a virtual network that is custom defined.
Amazon WorkSpaces is a fully managed, secure Desktop-as-a-Service (DaaS) solution, which runs on AWS.

Amazon WorkSpaces Applications is a fully managed solution to deliver software-as-a-service (SaaS) and web-based applications, and transform desktop applications into cloud-based services without code changes. It enables global scalability without infrastructure management and supports multi-session capabilities, optimizing resource use and costs across various user types.
AWS Application Auto Scaling is a web service for developers and system administrators to assist with the automatic scaling of resources for individual services beyond Amazon EC2.

AWS Application Migration Service (AWS MGN) minimizes time-intensive, error-prone manual processes by automatically converting customer source servers from physical, virtual, or cloud infrastructure to run natively on AWS. AWS Application Migration Service is the primary migration service recommended for lift-and-shift migrations to AWS.
