Type II examination of its Cloud Services and Cloud
Development Environment. It runs on Google Cloud
Platform and includes the infrastructure, software, data,
people and procedures that directly support Replit Agent,
the Cloud Development Environment and Replit
Deployments. Resources listed below are those likely to
handle federal customer data or to affect its confidentiality,
integrity or availability. Third-party services are described in
Section 8.
informationResources.explicitExclusions:
Replit mobile and desktop apps, which are software installed
on user devices and outside the scope of FedRAMP A. We
will plan to include this in scope as we move forward.
Internal corporate systems that do not support delivery of
the service, such as HR, payroll and recruiting tools.

resources.name: Google Cloud production infrastructure
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Google Kubernetes Engine, Compute Engine, Cloud
Storage, Cloud SQL and related Google Cloud services that
host all Replit services and store customer data.

resources.name: Replit web application and API
resources.descriptionAndRole:
The replit.com web application and GraphQL API that users
and administrators use to access the service.

resources.name: Cloud Development Environment runtime
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Isolated per-user microVMs and the control plane that create
and run cloud workspaces and store project files.

resources.name: Replit Agent and AI model proxy
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Services that run Replit Agent and route prompts and
workspace content to AI model providers.

resources.name: Replit Deployments hosting
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Infrastructure that builds and runs customer applications as
Reserved VM, Autoscale and Static deployments.

resources.name: User authentication services
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Firebase (Google Identity Platform) for user sign-in and
WorkOS for customer single sign-on.

resources.name: Key and secrets management
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Google Cloud KMS, Google Secret Manager and HashiCorp
Vault, which hold encryption keys and service secrets.
resources.impactOnConfidentialityIntegrityAvailabi:
Protects the confidentiality and integrity of customer data by
controlling the keys and secrets used to encrypt and access
it.

resources.name: Logging and monitoring
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Datadog, Sentry and Google Cloud logging, which collect
system logs, metrics, traces and error reports. Logs may
include customer data.

resources.name: Source control and CI/CD
resources.descriptionAndRole:
GitHub, Semaphore, Harness and Argo CD, which store
source code and deploy changes to production.
resources.impactOnConfidentialityIntegrityAvailabi:
Affects integrity and availability because these systems build
and deploy the code that runs the service.

resources.name: Workforce identity and device management
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Okta for workforce single sign-on and MFA, plus endpoint
management for employee devices.
resources.impactOnConfidentialityIntegrityAvailabi:
Affects confidentiality and integrity because it controls which
Replit personnel can access production systems.

resources.name: Replit operations and support personnel
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Security, SRE, engineering and support staff who operate
the service and respond to incidents and customer requests.

alternativeSecurityFramework.impactLevelScope:
SOC 2 Type II, Security Trust Services Criteria. System:
Replit Cloud Services and Cloud Development Environment.
Examination period: June 2, 2024 to October 31, 2025.
alternativeSecurityFramework.mappingToFedRampRules:
FRC-CSO-PKG and FRC-CSO-JSN: Replit is preparing this
package and the required JSON files with Paramify.
FRC-CSO-POP: Replit has selected the FedRAMP 20x path
and is not pursuing Rev5 for this offering.
MAS-CSO-IIR: Scope matches the SOC 2 system boundary.
See Section 6.
CDS-CSO-PUB and CDS-CSO-UTC: Public information and
certification data will be published through a FedRAMP-
compatible trust center on Paramify.
CDS-UTC-AAD: GRC owns a documented procedure to
notify FedRAMP within 5 business days of denying an
agency access request. See Section 2.
AFC-CSO-INB, AFC-CSO-RCV and AFC-CSO-CRA:
security@repl.it is the FedRAMP Security Inbox. It is a
shared inbox reviewed by the Security team, who will act on
FedRAMP Emergency and Emergency Test messages
within the stated timeframes.
IEC-CSO-EFR and IEC-CSO-FIR: Replit follows its Incident
Response Plan (v1.3, effective September 11, 2026), using
Rootly to log, track and communicate incidents. The SOC 2
auditor tested incident logging, tracking and communication
with no exceptions. Replit will add a step to evaluate
whether incidents affect federal customer data and will issue
Final Incident Reports within 3 business days of resolution.
VDR-CSO-DET: Replit scans source code and
dependencies, uses Wiz for cloud security and vulnerability
scanning, scans external-facing systems at least quarterly,
runs an annual third-party penetration test and operates a
private bug bounty program. Datadog and Cloudflare
provide intrusion detection. The SOC 2 auditor noted
exceptions in tracking critical and high findings to
remediation and in patch timing.
CCM-OCR-AVL and CCM-OCR-NRD: Replit will produce an
Ongoing Certification Report every 3 months and publish the
next report date.
IVV-CSX-AIA: Replit maintains an annual SOC 2 Type II
examination with Prescient Assurance. The current
examination period runs from November 1, 2025 to October
31, 2026.
KSI-CMT-LMC: Changes go through tickets, testing,
approval and version control, and CI/CD deployments are
logged and monitored with alerts. Tested by the SOC 2
auditor with no exceptions (CC7.2, CC8.1).
KSI-CNA-RNT: Production containers are firewalled and
external traffic enters only through designated HTTPS
frontends. Firewall rules are reviewed at least annually.
Tested with no exceptions (CC6.6).
KSI-CED-RAT: All employees complete security awareness
training in KnowBe4 within 30 days of hire and annually.
Tested with no exceptions (CC1.4, CC2.2).
KSI-IAM-AAM: Okta is the workforce identity provider, with
automated provisioning through SCIM for connected
applications. Access is removed within 24 hours of
termination and reviewed periodically. Tested with no
exceptions (CC6.2, CC6.3).
KSI-IAM-APM: Okta enforces single sign-on and MFA for in-
scope systems. Okta FastPass passwordless sign-in is
available. Tested with no exceptions (CC6.1, CC6.6).
KSI-INR-RIR: The Incident Response Plan requires at least
annual testing with lessons learned recorded. Annual
tabletop exercises were tested with no exceptions (CC7.4,
CC7.5).
KSI-SVC-SIN: Data is encrypted in transit with TLS and at
rest through Google Cloud encryption and Cloud KMS.
Backups are encrypted, access is role-based with SSO and
MFA, and customer data is deleted under a retention policy.
Tested with no exceptions (CC6.1 to CC6.6).

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
PDQ is an endpoint management platform designed for IT administrators and sysadmins. Manage, secure, and automate Windows and macOS endpoints across remote, hybrid, and on-site environments from a central platform.
PDQ is designed to make the grind of everyday IT workflows seamless and the thorny why-the-hell-isn’t-this-working issues easier to diagnose.
Core capabilities include patch management, vulnerability remediation, software deployment, remote desktop access and monitoring, and IT automation. In short, the stuff you actually tell us to build. Just look at our Discord.
Vulnerability remediation: Vulnerabilities are continuously detected and prioritized using real-world exploit activity in addition to CVSS, enabling remediation based on real, not theoretical, business risk.
Patch management: Patch Windows OS and more than 1,000 Windows and macOS packages from a hand-built library sourced directly from publishers, virus-scanned, stripped of nonsense, and typically updated within hours of a new release.
Software deployment and automation: PDQ's prebuilt workflows and automations can be running within minutes of onboarding. From there, sysadmins can combine custom multistep packages, advanced PowerShell Scanners, dynamic device groups, vulnerability automations, and a community-shared script library to create an end-to-end system tailor-built for their environment, reducing what was once days into minutes.
Remote desktop and diagnostics: For when all else fails, PDQ ships with native device-level diagnostics and a remote desktop tool that fires up quickly to help you diagnose, fix, and move on, whether you’re dealing with an x64 Lenovo or an ARM MacBook Pro.
Multitenant management: Multitenant support allows IT teams managing multiple environments to operate from a single console.
Real-time automation: Event-driven automation allows IT teams to execute workflows based on device state and predefined conditions. Deployments trigger the moment a condition is met without waiting for a scheduled window.
Offline device deployment: Offline device deployment queuing ensures no device is skipped, regardless of connectivity at the time a deployment runs.
Where compliance, regulatory, or org policy requires it, PDQ’s core deployment and patching capabilities can also be deployed as an on-premises, agentless solution.
PDQ is SOC 2 certified and includes security features such as MFA, role-based access controls, encryption, and audit logging to support compliance requirements.
Pricing is publicly available and supports self-service purchasing without requiring a sales call. A 14-day free trial is available with no credit card required.

Facility Grid is a multi-tenant SaaS platform for construction commissioning, quality control and turnover. Commissioning agents, general contractors and building owners use it to plan and record commissioning work on new and renovated buildings: equipment and system inventories, installation checklists, functional performance tests, issues and observations, schedules, documents, and the turnover package handed to the owner at completion.

**Federal use.** Facility Grid is used on federal construction and renovation projects delivered by prime contractors for the US Army Corps of Engineers, the Department of Veterans Affairs, the Department of Energy, the General Services Administration, the US Coast Guard and the Department of Homeland Security. On these projects the commissioning records are contract deliverables owned by the agency, and agency staff or agency-appointed commissioning agents use the platform to review and accept them.

**Scope.** This listing covers the Facility Grid commissioning platform (marketed as FG Construct): the web application, the REST API, and the server-side services behind the iOS and Android apps. It runs on Amazon Web Services in the commercial us-east-2 region. FG Validate and FG Sustain are separate products and are not part of this offering. The mobile apps are installed client software and are outside FedRAMP scope; the services they call are in scope.

**Certification path.** Facility Grid is pursuing a FedRAMP 20x Class A Certification for the existing commercial service on the strength of its SOC 2 Type II examination, and a Class C (Moderate) Certification afterwards, assessed by Insight Assurance.

KineticCode is a multi-tenant SaaS CI/CD governance platform that wraps GitHub-based software delivery with auditable controls for organizations handling sensitive and controlled information.

- **Pull-request gating:** required human approval, automated unit-test and coverage validation (including detection of empty or no-op tests), and automatic review.
- **Sensitive-data detection:** CUI/FCI marking assistance and detection of secrets, tokens and credentials in checked-in code, plus detection of risky code patterns.
- **Tamper evidence:** build checksums generated and re-verified at each environment promotion.
- **Controlled promotion:** strict sequential Dev, Test, Stage, Prod promotion with notifications on mismatch or stalled promotions.
- **Audit and evidence:** persistent audit trail of scans, approvals, merges and promotions, with a dashboard of pull requests, branches and environment status.
- **Access governance:** business-unit and role-based views, with detection and flagging of access-policy violations for human remediation.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
NorthWatch is a security assurance and visibility SaaS platform built to meet the reporting standards of FedRAMP 20x and the FedRAMP Consolidated Rules for 2026 (CR26).

It consists of the following services:

Key Security Indicators (KSI). This module presents the KSIs measured in a customer environment. It visualizes and reports the current and historical status of each KSI, and it provides the implementation, the validations, and a JSON summary of each KSI's source, measure and value. If the customer uses the NorthWatch validation engine, a validation agent is enrolled in the customer environment. The agent performs the KSI validations against the telemetry sources present there and reports the results to the NorthWatch service.

Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting (VER). This module ingests the customer's scan results by API, applies the defined security context of the customer system to each result, and derives the Potential Agency Impact N-rating (PAIN). The risk equation is automated from the factors in the VER ruleset and can be customized to capture the security context of the customer system. The module polls the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, the FIRST Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS), and the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD) to determine the exploitability of each identified vulnerability. It also accepts findings from other sources and applies the same contextual logic to them. It sets the remediation and mitigation SLAs from the PAIN rating, the likely exploitability, and the internet reachability of each vulnerability. The module records accepted vulnerabilities and their reporting requirements, the full vulnerability history, the remediation plans a customer authors in the module, and the mitigation activities taken to reduce risk.

Significant Change Notification (SCN). This module provides the form that meets the SCN reporting requirements for adaptive and transformative changes. It tracks each change through its lifecycle, collects evidence from third parties, and keeps a historical record of every change that meets the adaptive or transformative criteria. The module is built to take notifications from the customer's change-management system through its API, so the form is populated from that system rather than retyped. The notifications are published to the customer's assessor and agency customers through the Certification Data Sharing module as the twelve-month archive the ruleset requires.

Documents. This module is the customer's register of the governance documents FedRAMP 20x requires: policies, procedures, plans, inventories and records. Each document has a defined class with its required sections and accepted formats. A customer authors a document in the module, uploads one produced elsewhere, or has the module generate it from live system data (for example the certification package overview, the SCN twelve-month archive, the incident evaluation log and the quarterly review record). The module versions each document, checks its completeness and staleness against the rules, and lets the customer publish selected documents to its assessor and its agency customers as part of the signed certification package.

Certification Data Sharing (CDS). This module publishes the machine-readable JSON artifacts the FedRAMP rulesets define, each signed, together with a human-readable form. It is not a standalone service; it is the public face of the information held in the other modules: the certification package and its overview, the KSI summary, the SCN archive, the retained snapshot series, and the documents the customer has chosen to publish. Every artifact is reachable from a well-known discovery document on the customer's trust domain, so an assessor or an agency can find and verify it without an account.

Reporting. This module produces the reports the customer, its assessor and FedRAMP read, on a schedule or on demand. It includes the three FedRAMP vulnerability reports (Vulnerability Detail, Accepted Vulnerability Information, and Historical Activity) and the asset inventory, compliance, corrective action plan, detailed vulnerability, executive summary and trend analysis reports. A customer defines a report from these types with its own scope, format and schedule, and the module keeps the history of every run. Reports are produced as JSON, CSV, PDF or XLSX.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: 9line tells agencies which vulnerabilities in their software and AI supply chain actually affect them, with evidence an assessor can re-check. OcientAIQ™ is Ocient's ecosystem for running AI on petabyte-scale data sets in production. It combines proven solutions, expert delivery, and a platform built for speed, trust, and cost control.

At its core is the **OcientAIQ Unified Data Platform**, a petabyte-scale data foundation that sits between an organization's AI ecosystem and its enterprise data. serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
Optifi measures the WiFi experience of the devices an organization already manages and explains what is wrong when it is poor.

A small agent on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, ChromeOS and iOS devices, and optional fixed sensors, measure the wireless link, the local network, DNS, the internet path and chosen applications. The Optifi cloud service compares those measurements across devices, access points and sites, finds problems, names the likely cause (the device, the access point, the channel, the local network, DNS, the internet or an application) and checks whether a fix worked.

Optifi collects network measurements and device inventory (device name, serial number, operating system and network addresses). It does not collect the content of user traffic, browsing history or device location coordinates.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
The RediReview solution is delivered as a SaaS offering using a multi-tenant Government-Only Cloud computing environment hosted entirely in AWS GovCloud (US). 

RediReview is a benefits adjudication solution for federal programs and operations. It enables and assists agencies to make timely, accurate, and auditable adjudication decisions based on AI assisted document classification and analysis. The solution provides for secure ingestion of case files and related documents, that are processed post extraction, indexing, and classification of information. The information is then processed through a configurable agency-defined rules framework combined with AI to support adjudication decisions across a range of agency benefits. The result is faster, more consistent processing with less manual effort with complete audit trail. 

Each agency operates as a logically isolated tenant with its own data, configuration, and access controls. Tenants share certain common services within a single authorization boundary, including identity and access management, AI services, and data services, which is governed by one System Security Plan, one set of controls, and one continuous monitoring program. The platform runs containerized services in AWS GovCloud (US), organized into presentation, application, and data zones in a port-constrained network, with a separate management network for security monitoring, privileged access, and administration. AI processes run within the same GovCloud environment. Agency users authenticate through a single sign-on service with multi-factor authentication. Agency case files and data enter the boundary through two defined, secured ingress points, authenticated API interface with the agency system or secure retrieval from an encrypted storage bucket within AWS GovCloud (US). All logging and security events are collected for continuous monitoring.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription:
Octave Reliance (formerly ETQ Reliance) is a flexible and configurable enterprise Quality Management System (QMS) platform designed for government organizations and suppliers to design, implement and evolve quality processes to meet their unique and changing needs. With over 40 ready-to-use applications providing building blocks for robust, interconnected business processes, Octave Reliance serves as the backbone of a closed-loop quality ecosystem.


Measurable Value Across Critical Operations
The platform enables government agencies and their supply chains to deliver measurable value across critical operational areas:
Cost of Poor Quality – Reduce waste and rework through systematic quality controls (up to 32% or more reduction in scrap and rework achieved by global manufacturers)
Time to Market – Accelerate product delivery with automated workflows and streamlined processes (up to 80% improvement in new product introduction cycle times)
Supplier Quality – Strengthen supply chain resilience and compliance with complete visibility and control
Decision Velocity – Make faster, data-driven decisions with integrated analytics and predictive AI dashboards (customers have seen a 50% reduction in CAPA and SCAR resolution time)
Compliance at Scale – Maintain regulatory adherence across complex organizations with audit-ready workflows and automated recordkeeping
Proven Government & Defense Expertise
Trusted by hundreds of customers in manufacturing and service organizations and actively deployed across aerospace, defense and advanced manufacturing. With decades of service in regulated government and defense environments, Reliance is purpose-built for mission-critical quality operations. The platform supports complex supplier networks, stringent compliance requirements and the scalability needed for federal programs and global supply chains. Codeless configuration allows government teams to adapt processes without IT dependency.

 
Comprehensive Quality Capabilities
Octave Reliance provides integrated applications across the entire quality lifecycle:
Foundation & Governance – Document Control, Training Management, Audit Management, Quality Events
Problem Resolution & Prevention – Nonconformance Management, CAPA (Corrective Actions), Risk Assessment, Change Management
Supply Chain & Operations – Supplier Quality, Health & Safety, Environmental Management
Insights & Intelligence – Advanced Analytics, Predictive Dashboards, Real-time KPIs

All capabilities are integrated into a closed-loop ecosystem that reduces the cost of poor quality, accelerates time to market, strengthens supplier quality and ensures compliance at scale.


Enterprise-Grade Cloud Architecture
Built on AWS cloud infrastructure designed to support government and regulated industry requirements. ISO 27001 certified and compliant with 21 CFR Part 11, the platform provides role and location-based access control, comprehensive audit trails and encryption capabilities to protect sensitive quality and supplier data.

Government agencies trust Octave Reliance to modernize quality infrastructure while maintaining the operational resilience and governance required in defense and government operations.

serviceIdentification.serviceDescription:
RMPAC ONE is a software-as-a-service construction intelligence and management platform. One workspace carries a construction job from opportunity to closeout:

- **Find and win work:** federal opportunity search (SAM.gov), leads, a bid board, estimates by CSI division, bid packages sent to invited subcontractors, bid leveling and proposals.
- **Buy and deliver:** procurement buyout, purchase commitments, deliveries and supplier records.
- **Run the job:** submittals, RFIs, daily logs, punch lists, observations, changes, schedules, meetings, drawings and specifications, with photos and documents attached.
- **Manage the money:** schedules of values, budgets, AIA G702-style pay applications, cash flow, margin and certified payroll.
- **Review plans:** a PDF plan workspace for markups and measurements, and a takeoff tool that builds bills of materials from drawing sets by deterministic rules.
- **Ask questions:** an AI assistant that answers from the customer's own records. Prices researched on the web are shown with their source for a person to accept, change or ignore.

Intended agency use (Direct Use): federal facilities, engineering and acquisition staff who plan, procure, build, oversee and close out construction and renovation projects, used directly within an agency-authorized federal information system. Each agency authorizes its own use.

RMPAC ONE runs on Cloudflare (application hosting, database and file storage) and Amazon Web Services US East (identity, APIs, account database and document text extraction). See the third-party information resources below.

Write and test an incident response procedure, establish a monitored FedRAMP Security Inbox, and start security training for all staff (KSI-INR-RIR, KSI-CED-RAT).
Start persistent vulnerability detection and publish the Secure Configuration Guide (VDR-CSO-DET, SCG-CSO-RSC).
